docs.title: Audit evidence and explanations you don't have to translate yourself
docs.text:
WhiteBoxXAI packages what your AI actually did (SHAP, LIME and counterfactual explanations, bias audits, drift history, LLM audit trails, governance decisions) into evidence you can hand to an auditor or a board, with every number traceable to the data that produced it. It's also the monitoring platform your engineering team uses to produce that evidence in the first place.

Get started Generate a report Install the SDK

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• Getting Started

    Create an account, run the readiness setup, connect a model, and generate your first report.

  • The Enhanced Dashboard

    Overview, Needs Attention, Model Register, Assurance, Observability, Compliance & Evidence, Reviews & Decisions and the Risk Register: what each shows and how to use it.

  • Reports

    Board packs, ISO/IEC 42001 Statements of Applicability, EU AI Act Annex IV documentation, model cards and evidence packs, signed off and shared with auditors through verified links.

  • Python SDK

    Register models, log predictions and LLM calls from any provider, and group runs into Governance Events in a few lines.

  • MCP & AI agents

    Give Claude, Copilot, Cursor or your own agent 197 tools over your WhiteBoxXAI data, with agent skills that keep it honest.

  • Tutorials

    Explore with sample data, take a model to an evidence pack, govern an LLM app, or connect an assistant over MCP.

docs.title: What you can do with WhiteBoxXAI
docs.text:
• Explain every decision

    SHAP, LIME and DiCE counterfactuals computed from your model, so you can answer why a prediction was made and what would have changed it.

  • Audit for fairness

    Fairness audits across the groups you define, with per-group comparisons and the evidence regulators expect, not a summary of one.

  • Show compliance readiness

    Control catalogs for ISO/IEC 42001, the EU AI Act, GDPR, CCPA and NIST AI RMF, with your applicability decisions and approved evidence counted control by control. Compliance frameworks

  • Govern with confidence

    Review boards with votes signed by an authenticator code, separation of duties, and an immutable decision archive.

  • Track AI risk

    An AI Risk Register with owners, likelihood × impact scoring and a full audit trail, and a Trust Score per model a board can read.

  • Monitor LLMs, agents and models

    Drift, performance, LLM and RAG audit trails, safety scans, prompt versions and multi-agent workflows, with alert rules evaluated as new evidence arrives.

docs.title: Install the SDK
docs.text:
pip install whitebox-xai-sdk

import os

from whiteboxxai import WhiteBoxXAI

client = WhiteBoxXAI(api_key=os.environ["WHITEBOX_API_KEY"])

Then follow Getting Started to register a model and log your first predictions. AI agents can start from llms.txt.

docs.title: Compliance frameworks
docs.text:
WhiteBoxXAI covers five frameworks: ISO/IEC 42001, the EU AI Act, GDPR, CCPA and the NIST AI RMF. For each, it ships a control catalog, tracks your applicability decision and evidence for every control, and generates framework-specific reports.

What it doesn't do is just as important for an auditor to understand:

  • WhiteBoxXAI records evidence; it does not certify compliance. It shows which controls you've decided apply, which have approved evidence, and where the gaps are. Whether that evidence is sufficient is a judgement for your organization, your auditor or your regulator.
  • Readiness is a count, not a percentage. The dashboard says "18 of 25 controls evidenced", never "72% compliant", because a percentage invites a conclusion the evidence doesn't support.
  • Control titles are paraphrased summaries, not the operative text of the standard or regulation. Use the official text for audit-grade wording.
  • Other frameworks aren't covered. WhiteBoxXAI doesn't map evidence to HIPAA, SOC 2, US state AI laws or any framework not listed here.

Where to work with them: Compliance & Evidence for controls and evidence, and Reports for framework documents.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
Framework Catalog What's covered Framework reports ISO/IEC 42001:2023 63 controls, 16 groups Clauses 4–10 (AI management system requirements) and all 38 Annex A controls Statement of Applicability EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) 28 controls, 10 groups Provider and deployer obligations per AI system Annex IV Technical Documentation, Conformity Checklist GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) 25 controls, 4 groups Articles most relevant to AI on personal data Art. 35 DPIA / Art. 22 Automated-Decision Record CCPA, as amended by the CPRA 22 controls, 5 groups Automated decision-making technology (ADMT), risk assessments and consumer rights ADMT Risk Assessment NIST AI RMF 1.0 19 categories, 4 functions All 19 categories across GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE and MANAGE AI RMF Profile

The Quarterly Board Pack, Evidence Pack and Auditor Traceability Matrix span every framework you've adopted.

docs.title: ISO/IEC 42001
docs.text:
What's in the catalog: the AI management system requirements in clauses 4–10 (context, leadership, planning, support, operation, performance evaluation, improvement) and all 38 Annex A controls (A.2 to A.10), using the standard's own reference numbering.

What WhiteBoxXAI records:

  • applicability decisions and justifications for every control, which become the Statement of Applicability
  • evidence per control, with administrator approval
  • AIMS policies and guidelines (Clause 5) with an approval step, and measurable AI objectives (Clause 6.2), both recorded from the dashboard
  • assessments you record, and a readiness view by clause with open gaps
  • a downloadable certification package (JSON) for your certification body

Keep in mind: titles are summaries. You still need the licensed standard for audit-grade wording, and should check clause citations against your purchased copy before relying on them in a filing. WhiteBoxXAI doesn't certify you against ISO/IEC 42001; an accredited certification body does.

docs.title: EU AI Act
docs.text:
What's in the catalog: obligations an operator holds per AI system that a governance platform can evidence, in ten groups: AI literacy and prohibited practices; risk classification; risk management and data governance; technical documentation and record-keeping; human oversight and robustness; quality management and the AI value chain; deployer obligations; conformity assessment and registration; transparency and the right to explanation; and post-market monitoring and incident reporting.

The catalog follows Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by the Digital AI Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744). Application dates are phased:

Obligations Apply from AI literacy and prohibited practices (Articles 4 and 5) 2 February 2025 High-risk requirements (Articles 6–27) for Annex III systems 2 December 2027 High-risk requirements for Annex I systems 2 August 2028

These dates appear on the compliance calendar as regulatory dates, each with its citation and the date it was last checked.

What WhiteBoxXAI records:

  • a risk classification per AI system (unacceptable, high, limited or minimal)
  • conformity assessments and applicability decisions
  • the evidence Annex IV asks for: intended purpose, design, data governance and risk management measures, drawn from the system's register entry, audits and monitoring
  • explanations (SHAP, LIME, DiCE counterfactuals) that support transparency and the right to explanation

Not covered: regulator, member-state and notified-body provisions, and the general-purpose AI model rules (Articles 51–56), which apply to models rather than to each AI system. Confirm current applicability for your organization before relying on the catalog in a filing.

docs.title: GDPR
docs.text:
What's in the catalog: the articles a model-governance platform can meaningfully evidence: principles and lawfulness, transparency and data-subject rights, accountability and design (including DPIAs and Article 22 automated decision-making), and breach notification. It is not a complete GDPR compliance program.

What WhiteBoxXAI records:

  • data subject requests, including Article 22 automated-decision requests, newest first
  • Article 30 processing records
  • a breach register
  • consent records as evidence
  • explanations of individual automated decisions

docs.title: CCPA
docs.text:
What's in the catalog: CCPA/CPRA sections and CPPA regulations relevant to automated decision-making technology (ADMT) and the risk assessments the CPPA requires for it, plus consumer rights. It follows the Civil Code as amended effective 1 January 2026 and the CPPA's approved regulations.

What WhiteBoxXAI records:

  • consumer requests
  • ADMT applicability decisions and risk-assessment evidence
  • fairness audits and explanations for the automated decisions in scope

docs.title: NIST AI RMF
docs.text:
What's in the catalog: the framework's 19 categories across its four functions: GOVERN (6), MAP (5), MEASURE (4) and MANAGE (4). WhiteBoxXAI works at category level rather than the 72 subcategories, because most subcategories are organizational practices a platform can't evidence itself.

The NIST AI RMF is voluntary. No category is mandatory, and "in scope" means you have declared it in scope, not that it's a legal requirement.

What WhiteBoxXAI records:

  • applicability decisions per category, which become the AI RMF Profile
  • open risks per function, from the AI Risk Register
  • the measurement evidence for MEASURE: drift, fairness, explainability and LLM safety results

docs.title: One artifact, several frameworks
docs.text: Most evidence counts towards more than one framework. A bias audit report, for example, maps to controls in all five. File it once, and Compliance & Evidence → Controls → Evidence by artifact shows every control it supports. See Compliance & Evidence.

docs.title: From code and agents
docs.text:
frameworks = client.compliance.list_frameworks()      # key, name, total_controls, adopted, next_audit_date
controls = client.compliance.get_framework_controls("iso_42001")   # gdpr, ccpa, eu_ai_act, nist_ai_rmf
client.compliance.iso42001_score()
client.compliance.iso42001_gaps(severity_filter="high")

The MCP server exposes the same data (whitebox_compliance_* tools), and the compliance-evidence skill tells an AI assistant to report unassessed controls as "not yet assessed" rather than estimating a result.

docs.title: API Keys
docs.text:
API keys are the credential your code uses to talk to WhiteBoxXAI. They're individually revocable, and don't expire on a fixed schedule — which makes them the right choice for the SDK, CI/CD pipelines, the MCP server, and anything else running unattended.

Keys look like this:

wbx_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

docs.title: In the dashboard
docs.text:
Go to Settings → API keys (administrators only), create a key, give it a name and optional expiry, and copy it. Non-administrators see who their administrators are instead.

The list shows each key's prefix, expiry and when it was last used, with Revoke.

docs.title: Via the API
docs.text:
Key creation and revocation are admin-only, because an API key is an organization-wide credential rather than a personal one.

curl -X POST https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/api-keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "CI pipeline — nightly drift job",
    "scopes": ["read", "write"],
    "expires_in_days": 365
  }'
Field Notes name Required, max 255 characters. Make it descriptive — it's how you'll identify the key later. scopes Optional list of labels, e.g. ["read", "write"]. Recorded with the key, but not yet enforced (see below). expires_in_days Optional, 1–3650. Omit for a key that never expires.

The 201 response is the only time you see the key material:

{
  "id": "a1b2c3d4-...",
  "name": "CI pipeline — nightly drift job",
  "key_prefix": "wbx_live_a1b2c3d4...",
  "scopes": ["read", "write"],
  "expires_at": "2027-07-29T00:00:00Z",
  "last_used_at": null,
  "revoked_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-07-29T00:00:00Z",
  "raw_key": "wbx_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
}

raw_key is shown exactly once

Store it immediately in your secrets manager. WhiteBoxXAI keeps only a hash and the prefix — the full key cannot be retrieved again. If you lose it, revoke the key and issue a new one.

docs.title: Use a key
docs.text:
Send it as a bearer token:

curl https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer wbx_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"

With the Python SDK:

from whiteboxxai import WhiteBoxXAI

client = WhiteBoxXAI(api_key="wbx_live_...")

Or, preferably, from the environment:

export WHITEBOX_API_KEY="wbx_live_..."

import os

client = WhiteBoxXAI(api_key=os.environ["WHITEBOX_API_KEY"])

docs.title: List keys
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/api-keys

Returns every key in your organization with its metadata — never the key material, only the key_prefix for identification. last_used_at tells you whether a key is still in service, which is what you want before revoking one.

docs.title: Revoke a key
docs.text:
DELETE /api/v1/api-keys/{key_id}

Returns 204. Revocation is immediate — any process still using that key starts getting 401 on its next request. Revoke a key as soon as you suspect exposure; unlike a password, there's nothing else to rotate.

docs.title: What a key can do
docs.text:
An API key acts with the permissions of the administrator who created it, inside that administrator's organization. If that person is deactivated, their keys stop working.

Scopes you set when creating a key are recorded with it, but they aren't enforced per request yet, so a key can do anything its creator can. Treat every key as an administrator credential: one key per consumer, expiry dates for temporary access, and revoke anything you don't recognise.

Two things a key can never do:

  • Vote on, or finalize, a governance review request. Votes need a person's own session with two-factor authentication and an authenticator code. See Reviews & Decisions.
  • Act in another organization. A request for another organization's record returns 404.

Requests made with a key are the ones metered as Governance Events; using the dashboard is not.

docs.title: API keys vs. login tokens
docs.text:
The Authorization: Bearer header accepts either an API key or a login JWT from POST /api/v1/auth/login. They are not equivalent:

API key Login JWT Lifetime Until you revoke it (or its optional expiry) ~30 minutes Permissions Those of the administrator who created it, in their organization Those of the signed-in person Revocable individually Yes No — you'd rotate the account's credentials Good for SDK, CI/CD, pipelines, MCP server, webhooks Quick interactive scripts, the dashboard

Use a JWT for a throwaway script if it's convenient. Use an API key for anything that runs without a person watching it — a 30-minute token in a nightly job is a job that fails at minute 31.

docs.title: Keys and two-factor authentication
docs.text:
Two-factor authentication protects interactive dashboard logins. It does not affect API keys — a key authenticates on its own, with no 2FA challenge. Enabling 2FA won't break your existing integrations, and no code changes are needed.

The practical consequence: an API key is a standalone credential, so treat it with the same care as a password. Keep keys out of source control, out of notebooks you share, and out of log output.

docs.title: Good practice
docs.text:
• One key per consumer. A separate key for each pipeline, environment, and service means you can revoke one without taking down everything else.
  • Name keys after where they run. "CI pipeline — nightly drift job" beats "key 3" when you're deciding six months later whether it's safe to revoke.
  • Set an expiry for temporary access. Contractors, spikes, and one-off migrations should get a key with expires_in_days.
  • Check last_used_at before revoking. And revoke anything that hasn't been used in a while — an unused key is pure risk.
  • Store keys in a secrets manager, not in .env files that get committed. See Secure configuration.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
401 Unauthorized: Invalid API key

Check that the key hasn't been revoked or expired (GET /api/v1/api-keys shows revoked_at and expires_at), that you copied the whole key, and that your environment variable is actually set in the process making the request.

403 Forbidden on a request that should work

Check whether the administrator who created the key still has the administrator role, and whether the request is one that keys can't make by design, such as voting on a governance review. If you've reached your plan's Governed AI Systems limit, registering a model under a new name also returns 403.

403 when creating a key

Key creation is admin-only. Ask an organization admin to issue it.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Two-Factor Authentication
  • MCP Server — uses an API key via WHITEBOXXAI_MCP_API_KEY.
  • SDK Authentication

docs.title: Single Sign-On (Microsoft Entra ID)
docs.text:
When an auditor asks who can reach your AI governance evidence, "everyone with a password we issued" is a hard answer to defend. Single sign-on moves that control to your identity provider: people sign in with their Microsoft work account, and leaving the company or the directory removes their access.

WhiteBoxXAI supports Microsoft Entra ID (OpenID Connect). It is available on Business Cloud and above; it isn't part of the Free plan. See Plans & Limits.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need three things in place:

  • The WhiteBoxXAI admin role. Only administrators can see or change the connection.
  • Two-factor authentication turned on for your own account. Starting the connection without it returns "Enable two-factor authentication before connecting single sign-on."
  • A Microsoft account that is a Global Administrator, Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator in your Entra tenant. Connecting grants consent for the whole tenant, and WhiteBoxXAI checks the administrator role in the sign-in token. A regular member account is refused.

docs.title: Connect Entra ID
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings → Single sign-on.
  2. Click Connect Microsoft Entra ID.
  3. Sign in with the Microsoft administrator account and approve the consent request.

WhiteBoxXAI takes your tenant from the signed Microsoft token, not from a value you type.

docs.title: What people see
docs.text: Once connected, the sign-in page offers Sign in with your organisation. It starts the Microsoft sign-in and returns the person to WhiteBoxXAI.

docs.title: Accounts and roles
docs.text:
Setting What it does Create accounts on first sign-in On (the default): a person with a valid Microsoft sign-in gets a WhiteBoxXAI account the first time they arrive. Off: only people an administrator has already added can sign in. Role when Microsoft sends none The role given when the sign-in carries no app role: viewer (the default), analyst or admin. Role mapping Maps the Microsoft app role on the sign-in to a WhiteBoxXAI role. The defaults are WhiteBox.Admin → admin, WhiteBox.Analyst → analyst and WhiteBox.Viewer → viewer. You can change the mapping.

A member's role follows their Microsoft app role each time they sign in. Change it in Entra and it takes effect at their next sign-in.

An existing WhiteBoxXAI account is linked to its Microsoft identity only when Microsoft reports the email domain as verified. This stops someone with an unverified address from taking over an account that already exists.

docs.title: Require SSO
docs.text:
By default, SSO is an option alongside passwords. Require SSO makes it the only way in.

Turning it on refuses, for every member except the break-glass administrators below:

  • password sign-in
  • the password-and-two-factor flow
  • the email-verification sign-in link
  • social sign-in
  • password reset

Sessions that are already open end within 30 minutes. API keys are not affected, so SDK and MCP integrations keep working.

WhiteBoxXAI won't let you turn it on until:

  • the connection is active,
  • at least one break-glass administrator is chosen, and
  • you have signed in with SSO yourself at least once. Otherwise you could lock yourself out with a configuration that doesn't work.

docs.title: Break-glass administrators
docs.text: If Entra is down or misconfigured, nobody can sign in with SSO. Break-glass administrators are the exception: they keep password and two-factor sign-in while Require SSO is on. Only organization administrators with two-factor authentication enabled can be chosen. Pick more than one if you can, and test their password sign-in before you need it.

docs.title: For integrators
docs.text:
The connection is managed through these endpoints, which require an administrator on a plan that includes SSO. See the REST API Reference.

Method Path Notes GET /api/v1/sso/connection Read the connection POST /api/v1/sso/connection/entra/start Begin the Entra connect flow PATCH /api/v1/sso/connection Change JIT, default role, role mapping, Require SSO DELETE /api/v1/sso/connection Remove the connection GET /api/v1/sso/entra/login Start a sign-in (public) GET /api/v1/sso/entra/callback Microsoft redirect target (public)

docs.title: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
docs.text:
Two-factor authentication adds a second layer of security to your WhiteBoxXAI account. In addition to your password, you'll enter a short code from an authenticator app when you log in — so your account stays protected even if your password is ever compromised.

WhiteBoxXAI uses TOTP (time-based one-time passwords), the same standard supported by apps like Google Authenticator, Authy, Microsoft Authenticator, and 1Password.

Recommended for every account

We strongly recommend enabling 2FA — and requiring it for any administrator accounts in your organization.

docs.title: Enable 2FA
docs.text:
1. Log in and go to Settings → Profile & security.
  2. Click Enable Two-Factor Authentication.
  3. Scan the QR code with your authenticator app. (Prefer not to scan? Enter the setup key shown beneath the code manually.)
  4. Enter the current 6-digit code from your app and click Verify and Enable.
  5. Save your backup codes — download or print them and store them somewhere safe (a password manager is ideal). Each code can be used once.

Your account is now protected with 2FA.

docs.title: Log in with 2FA
docs.text:
1. Enter your email and password as usual.
  2. When prompted, open your authenticator app and enter the current 6-digit code.
  3. Click Verify.

Codes rotate every 30 seconds, so always enter the one currently shown.

docs.title: Use a backup code
docs.text:
If you don't have your authenticator app handy — for example, you've replaced your phone — you can log in with a backup code:

  1. Enter your email and password.
  2. On the 2FA prompt, choose Use a backup code.
  3. Enter one of your saved backup codes.
  4. Once logged in, go to Settings → Profile & security and set up your authenticator again.

You can regenerate a fresh set of backup codes at any time from Settings → Profile & security; generating new codes invalidates the old set.

docs.title: Disable 2FA
docs.text: Go to Settings → Profile & security → Disable two-factor authentication and confirm with your password. We only recommend this if you're switching to a new device — re-enable 2FA as soon as you can.

docs.title: API keys and 2FA
docs.text:
2FA protects interactive logins to the dashboard. It does not affect API keys, so your SDK and API integrations keep working without any changes.

The flip side is that an API key is a standalone credential — 2FA won't protect it. Keep keys secret, and revoke any key you suspect has been exposed; revocation is immediate.

The MCP server authenticates with an API key, so it works with 2FA on.

docs.title: Lost access to your account?
docs.text: If you've lost both your authenticator app and your backup codes, contact support@whiteboxxai.com. Account recovery requires identity verification and may take 24–48 hours, so keep your backup codes safe.

docs.title: Governance votes need a code
docs.text: Voting on, or finalizing, a governance review request requires two-factor authentication to be on and a current authenticator code (or a backup code) for each vote. This is separate from sign-in: it proves that the vote was cast by you, at that moment. API keys can't vote. See Reviews & Decisions.

docs.title: Agent & Developer Resources
docs.text: WhiteBoxXAI is used by people and by the AI agents working for them. This section collects the entry points an agent needs to set up WhiteBoxXAI, call it correctly, and report what it returned without inventing anything.

docs.title: Start here (for agents)
docs.text:
Resource URL Use it to Docs index for LLMs https://docs.whiteboxxai.com/llms.txt Find the right docs page without crawling the whole site Agent skills index https://whiteboxxai.com/skills/index.md Pick which skill to load for a task Skills discovery (JSON) https://whiteboxxai.com/.well-known/skills/index.json Auto-discover and verify skills in a harness All skills (zip) https://whiteboxxai.com/skills/whitebox-skills.zip Install every skill at once MCP server MCP Server Give an assistant live tools over the user's WhiteBoxXAI data Compliance-assistant prompt AI Prompts Bootstrap an assistant that summarises evidence for a risk officer Client config files Agent Config Definitions Copy-paste MCP client configuration

The fastest way to get a coding agent going is to paste this instruction into it:

Read https://whiteboxxai.com/.well-known/skills/whitebox-getting-started/SKILL.md and set up WhiteBoxXAI for this repository.

docs.title: Which integration path?
docs.text: You are... Use Docs Instrumenting Python code that trains or serves a model Python SDK SDK guide Instrumenting an LLM app, RAG pipeline or agent Python SDK LLM monitoring, Multi-agent monitoring An assistant that should query or act on WhiteBoxXAI for a user MCP server MCP Server Working in a language other than Python REST API under /api/v1/ API Reference

docs.title: Rules for agents
docs.text:
These are the same rules the whitebox-governance-rules skill enforces. They exist because WhiteBoxXAI output becomes compliance evidence that a person may hand to an auditor.

  1. Never invent a number. If a call returns nothing, an error, or an unassessed state, say exactly that. A wrong score presented as a result is worse than no score.
  2. Put a plain-language verdict next to every ML number, using the platform's own verdict when it returns one. Don't present your own pass/fail threshold as the platform's.
  3. Keep secrets out of code. Read the key from the environment (WHITEBOX_API_KEY for the SDK, WHITEBOXXAI_MCP_API_KEY for the MCP server). Keys look like wbx_live_....
  4. A 404 means "not in your organization". Don't retry with other credentials or guess ids.
  5. Human decisions stay human. Governance votes need a person's own session, two-factor authentication and an authenticator code. An organization API key is refused. Prepare and summarise the dossier; never vote on someone's behalf.
  6. Stay inside the five frameworks: ISO/IEC 42001, GDPR, CCPA, the EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF. WhiteBoxXAI records evidence; it does not certify compliance.
  7. Meter responsibly. Group one AI run's records with governance_run() and honour Retry-After on a 429. See Governance Events.

docs.title: AI Prompts
docs.text: Use these system prompts to start an assistant that works with WhiteBoxXAI. Pair them with the agent skills: the prompt sets behaviour, and the skills supply the exact calls.

docs.title: Compliance assistant
docs.text:
For an assistant that answers a compliance or risk officer's questions from their WhiteBoxXAI data, usually through the MCP server. Also published at whiteboxxai.com/prompts/compliance_assistant.md.

You are a compliance assistant working with a customer's WhiteBoxXAI data. The person you are
helping is usually a compliance or risk officer, not an ML engineer.

Setup: load these skills before you act: whitebox-governance-rules (always), then
whitebox-compliance-evidence, and whitebox-getting-started if WhiteBoxXAI is not yet connected.
They are listed at https://whiteboxxai.com/skills/index.md.

1. Answer from what WhiteBoxXAI actually returned. If a call returns nothing, an error, or an
   unassessed state, say exactly that.
2. Never state a metric, score or percentage that was not returned by a call you made. If a metric
   has not been computed, say it has not been computed.
3. Lead every finding with a plain-language verdict, then the evidence (ids, report names, dates).
4. Stay within ISO/IEC 42001, GDPR, CCPA, the EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF. WhiteBoxXAI records
   evidence; it does not certify compliance.
5. Never cast a governance vote. Prepare and summarise the dossier for the human reviewer.

docs.title: Developer assistant
docs.text:
For a coding agent that adds WhiteBoxXAI instrumentation to a repository. Put it in the agent's system instructions or in the repository's agent instructions file.

You are adding WhiteBoxXAI monitoring and governance to this codebase.

Setup: load whitebox-governance-rules and whitebox-getting-started from
https://whiteboxxai.com/skills/index.md, then the skill that matches the system
(whitebox-register-and-monitor-models for ML models, whitebox-llm-and-agent-observability for
LLM, RAG and agent apps).

1. Use the official Python SDK (pip install whitebox-xai-sdk; import whiteboxxai). Don't hand-roll
   HTTP calls when the SDK has the method.
2. Read the API key from the WHITEBOX_API_KEY environment variable. Never write a key into source,
   notebooks, committed config or logs.
3. Log what the model actually received and returned. Never estimate token counts, costs or
   metrics, and only pass baseline metrics that came from a real evaluation.
4. Wrap each end-to-end AI run in governance_run() so its records share Governance Events.
5. On a 429, wait for Retry-After. On a 404 for an id, treat it as "not in this organization".
6. Never invent a number when a call returns nothing. Report the empty result.

docs.title: Generating reports from an agent
docs.text:
Report types are discovered at runtime, not hard-coded:

types = client.reports.list()            # pick an id from this list
result = client.reports.generate(report_type_id="model_card", model_id=model_id, format="pdf")

See Report types reference for what each report contains.

docs.title: Agent Skills
docs.text:
Agent skills are SKILL.md files that teach a coding agent how to use WhiteBoxXAI correctly: which SDK calls and MCP tools exist, what their arguments mean, and what the agent must never do (invent a score, commit a key, cast a governance vote). Each skill has a TRIGGER / SKIP description so the agent loads it only when it applies.

All skills are MIT-licensed, published by AgentaFlow, and checked against the current SDK and MCP tool list before release.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Pick one:

Paste into your agentSkills CLIZip download 
Read https://whiteboxxai.com/.well-known/skills/whitebox-getting-started/SKILL.md and set up WhiteBoxXAI for this repository.

npx skills add https://whiteboxxai.com

Lists every skill and installs the ones you pick.

Download whitebox-skills.zip and unzip it into your agent's skills directory, for example .claude/skills/ or .agents/skills/.

Harnesses that support skill discovery can read the index at https://whiteboxxai.com/.well-known/skills/index.json. Each entry carries a SHA-256 digest so the harness can verify the file it downloads.

docs.title: The skills
docs.text:
Always load whitebox-governance-rules alongside any other WhiteBoxXAI skill.

Skill Load it when the user wants to... Skip it when... whitebox-getting-started Add or connect WhiteBoxXAI: install the SDK or MCP server, set an API key, choose an integration path WhiteBoxXAI is already configured whitebox-governance-rules Do anything that reads from or writes to WhiteBoxXAI The work never touches WhiteBoxXAI whitebox-register-and-monitor-models Register and log predictions for scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, PyTorch, TensorFlow/Keras or Hugging Face models The system is an LLM, RAG or agent app whitebox-drift-alerts-explainability Check drift, set alert rules, explain predictions with SHAP/LIME, run a fairness audit The model isn't registered yet whitebox-llm-and-agent-observability Log LLM calls, RAG retrievals, safety checks and multi-agent workflows; version, deploy and roll back prompts; group a run into one Governance Event The system is a tabular ML model whitebox-mcp-server Connect an assistant, IDE or agent harness over MCP, or pick the right MCP tool Instrumenting application code (use the SDK skills) whitebox-compliance-evidence Summarise ISO/IEC 42001 readiness, the risk register, review dossiers, or reports for a risk officer or auditor The request needs a legal conclusion

The full index with descriptions is at whiteboxxai.com/skills/index.md.

docs.title: What the skills enforce
docs.text:
The skills say more than "how to call the API". They also carry the rules a compliance team depends on:

  • Report empty, errored or unassessed results as they are, never as a default value.
  • Put a plain-language verdict beside every drift statistic, fairness metric or explanation weight.
  • Read keys from the environment; never write one into source, notebooks or logs.
  • Treat a 404 on an id as "not in this organization", not as an outage.
  • Never cast a governance vote on a person's behalf.
  • Stay within ISO/IEC 42001, GDPR, CCPA, the EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF.

See Agent & Developer Resources for the other agent entry points.

docs.title: Agent Config Definitions
docs.text: Machine-readable configuration for connecting agents to WhiteBoxXAI. Replace wbx_live_... with an API key from Settings → API keys in the dashboard, and use your client's secret or input mechanism for it where one exists. Don't commit the key.

docs.title: MCP server: local (stdio)
docs.text:
The whiteboxxai-mcp command runs the server on your machine and talks to WhiteBoxXAI with your API key. Install it with pip install whiteboxxai-mcp (Python 3.11 or later).

Most MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf) use this JSON shape:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "whiteboxxai": {
      "command": "whiteboxxai-mcp",
      "env": {
        "WHITEBOXXAI_MCP_API_BASE_URL": "https://api.whiteboxxai.com",
        "WHITEBOXXAI_MCP_API_KEY": "wbx_live_..."
      }
    }
  }
}

The same definition as YAML, for harnesses that take YAML:

mcpServers:
  whiteboxxai:
    command: whiteboxxai-mcp
    env:
      WHITEBOXXAI_MCP_API_BASE_URL: https://api.whiteboxxai.com
      WHITEBOXXAI_MCP_API_KEY: ${WHITEBOXXAI_MCP_API_KEY}

Download: whiteboxxai-mcp.yaml

Client-specific variants (VS Code's servers key, the Claude Code CLI, remote HTTP) are on the MCP Server page.

docs.title: MCP server: hosted (Streamable HTTP)
docs.text:
Clients that support remote MCP servers can connect to WhiteBoxXAI's hosted endpoint without installing anything. Every request needs an Authorization header.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "whiteboxxai": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.whiteboxxai.com/mcp/",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer wbx_live_..."
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: n8n webhook node
docs.text:
A starting point for an n8n workflow that receives WhiteBoxXAI alert notifications on a webhook. This is a single n8n Webhook node definition shown in YAML for readability; n8n imports workflows as JSON, so convert it (or build the node in the n8n editor with the same settings). Point a WhiteBoxXAI webhook notification channel at the URL n8n gives you. See n8n Webhooks for sending n8n execution data to WhiteBoxXAI.

name: WhiteBoxXAI Alert Listener
nodes:
  - name: Webhook
    type: n8n-nodes-base.webhook
    typeVersion: 1
    position: [250, 300]
    parameters:
      httpMethod: POST
      path: whitebox-alerts
      responseMode: lastNode
      options: {}

Download: n8n-alert-webhook.yaml

docs.title: Getting Started with WhiteBoxXAI
docs.text:
An auditor, a regulator or your own review board will eventually ask how a production AI system behaves and who signed off on it. This guide gets you from a new account to a monitored model with evidence you could hand over: real predictions logged, drift and explanations computed from them, and a report generated from the result.

It takes about 20 minutes. Prefer to explore first? Load sample data (step 2) and skip to Find your way around.

Using an AI coding agent?

Give it this instruction and it can do steps 3 to 5 for you: Read https://whiteboxxai.com/.well-known/skills/whitebox-getting-started/SKILL.md and set up WhiteBoxXAI for this repository. See Agent Skills.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Python 3.9 or later, if you'll connect a model with the SDK
  • A model you can call: scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, PyTorch, TensorFlow/Keras, Hugging Face, an LLM app, or anything else you can call from Python

No Python? You can still register models, review evidence, run the readiness setup and generate reports entirely from the dashboard.

docs.title: 1. Create your account
docs.text:
1. Go to whiteboxxai.com and choose Get Started for Free.
  2. Sign up with Google or Microsoft, or with email. The email form asks for:
    • Full Name
    • Email
    • Password: at least 10 characters, with at least one letter and one number
    • Confirm Password
  3. Optionally tick the box to receive product updates. You can change this later in Settings → Data & privacy.
  4. Click Create Account. If you're asked to verify your email, follow the link we send.

You're the Administrator of a new organization on the Free plan: one Governed AI System and 2,500 Governance Events a month. You can invite colleagues later from Settings → Users & roles.

Turn on two-factor authentication now

Two-factor authentication protects the account that will hold your compliance evidence. You'll also need it to vote on governance review requests. Go to Settings → Profile & security. See Two-Factor Authentication.

docs.title: 2. Set up compliance readiness
docs.text:
The first time you sign in, WhiteBoxXAI opens on the Enhanced Dashboard and offers Set up your compliance readiness. You can also start it any time from Overview → Set up readiness.

The setup has five steps. Each step is checked against your real data, not a checkbox you tick:

  1. Frameworks: adopt the frameworks you're accountable to: ISO/IEC 42001, the EU AI Act, GDPR, CCPA, or NIST AI RMF.
  2. Audit dates: set your next audit date for each framework. It appears on the compliance calendar and drives deadline reminders.
  3. Applicability: review the default decisions about which controls apply to you.
  4. Connect the SDK: send real data from a model (steps 3 to 5 below).
  5. Invite a reviewer: invite a colleague who will review and approve AI changes.

Your progress shows on the Overview as Your readiness setup: N of 5 steps done. Analysts can propose framework adoptions and dates, and an administrator confirms them.

Want to see a populated dashboard first?

Go to Settings → Sample data & tour → Load sample data. Sample models, predictions, drift events, bias audits and reports are added and clearly marked as sample data. They don't count against your plan, and Reset sample data removes them. WhiteBoxXAI never shows invented numbers on your own systems: an account with no data shows empty states.

docs.title: 3. Install the SDK and create an API key
docs.text:
pip install whitebox-xai-sdk

Optional extras install framework integrations: whitebox-xai-sdk[sklearn], [pytorch], [tensorflow], [xgboost], [lightgbm], [huggingface], [langchain], or [all].

Create an API key in Settings → API keys (administrators only). Copy it when it's shown; it's displayed once. Keys look like wbx_live_.... Then put it in your environment rather than in code:

macOS / LinuxWindows PowerShell 
export WHITEBOX_API_KEY="wbx_live_..."

$env:WHITEBOX_API_KEY = "wbx_live_..."

Check the connection:

import os

from whiteboxxai import WhiteBoxXAI

client = WhiteBoxXAI(api_key=os.environ["WHITEBOX_API_KEY"])
print(client.models.list(limit=5))

An authentication error means the key is wrong or revoked. See API Keys.

Business Cloud

On Business Cloud, your organization has its own tenant. Use the API address you were given when the tenant was set up, by passing base_url= or setting WHITEBOX_BASE_URL.

docs.title: 4. Register a model and log predictions
docs.text:
Register the model once. Calling register again with the same name and version returns the existing model, so it's safe to run on every start-up.

model = client.models.register(
    name="credit_scoring",
    model_type="xgboost",          # xgboost, random_forest, neural_network, linear_model, llm or custom
    framework="xgboost",
    version="1.0.0",
    features=["income", "utilisation", "tenure_months"],
    baseline_metrics={"accuracy": 0.94},   # only values you actually measured; {} if none
    auto_detect_git=True,          # records the commit and branch the model came from
)
model_id = model["id"]

Then log what the model actually received and returned:

client.predictions.log(
    model_id=model_id,
    input_data={"income": 52000, "utilisation": 0.31, "tenure_months": 18},
    output_data={"prediction": 0, "probability": 0.12},
    latency_ms=4.2,
)

Rather not call log yourself? Wrap the model and every prediction is logged for you:

from whiteboxxai.integrations.sklearn import SklearnMonitor, SklearnWrapper

monitor = SklearnMonitor(client, model=clf)          # clf: your fitted estimator
monitor.register_from_model(
    name="credit_scoring",
    model_type="random_forest",
    version="1.0.0",
    features=["income", "utilisation", "tenure_months"],
    baseline_metrics={},
)
wrapped = SklearnWrapper(clf, monitor)
wrapped.predict(X)               # logged automatically

Integrations exist for XGBoost, LightGBM, PyTorch, TensorFlow/Keras and Hugging Face too. See SDK & API. For LLM, RAG and agent apps, see LLM monitoring.

Log only what you need

Log the features the model uses. Don't log names, addresses or government ids. Put a non-identifying reference such as a customer id in metadata if you need to trace a decision.

Each logged prediction is one Governance Event. For very high-volume models, log a representative sample, or group related records into runs.

You can also register a model without code: Model Register → Register a system.

docs.title: 5. Find your way around
docs.text:
Open the Enhanced Dashboard. The sidebar is grouped by what you're trying to do:

Area What you'll find Overview Where your AI systems stand: trust score, open findings, framework readiness, and what changed Needs Attention Every alert, risk, review and deadline that needs a person, worst first Model Register Every AI system you govern, with a dossier per system Assurance Explainability, fairness and drift for a system Observability Runtime performance, LLM & RAG activity, agents and prompt evaluations Compliance & Evidence Frameworks, controls, evidence, reports, the compliance calendar and the audit trail Reviews & Decisions Review requests, boards, votes and the decision archive Risk Register Your AI risks, scored by likelihood and impact

Press ⌘K (or Ctrl+K) to search systems, controls, reports and reviews, and ? to see keyboard shortcuts. Choose Take the product tour from the ⌘K menu for a guided walkthrough.

docs.title: 6. Check drift and explain a prediction
docs.text:
Once predictions are flowing, ask for evidence computed from them:

report = client.drift.create_report(model_id, window_size=1000)   # stored, citable by id
explanation = client.explanations.generate(
    model_id,
    instance={"income": 52000, "utilisation": 0.31, "tenure_months": 18},
    method="shap",
)

Explanations run the model itself, so they need the model file stored with WhiteBoxXAI: register the model through GitHub with storage_mode: full. With metadata-only registration, as in step 4, drift and fairness work but explanation requests are recorded as failed.

Or use Assurance in the dashboard, which shows each result with a plain-language verdict and a How was this computed? note. With little or no data, WhiteBoxXAI says the result can't be computed yet rather than showing a number. Drift needs a meaningful window of predictions to compare against the baseline.

See Assurance.

docs.title: 7. Generate your first report
docs.text:
1. Go to Compliance & Evidence → Reports.
  2. Pick a report type: for example Model Card, Drift Report or Quarterly Board Pack. Each card says whether it's Ready or what data it still needs.
  3. Choose PDF, Word (DOCX) or HTML and click Generate.

The report is saved to History, where you can download it, record Preparer / Reviewer / Approver sign-off, or share it with an auditor through a verified, expiring link.

From code:

types = client.reports.list()            # pick a report type id from this list
result = client.reports.generate(report_type_id="drift_report", model_id=model_id, format="pdf")

See Reports.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
Set up governance

  • Compliance & Evidence: adopt frameworks, decide control applicability and attach evidence
  • Reviews & Decisions: review boards and approval workflows
  • AI Risk Register and Trust Score

Instrument more systems

  • LLM monitoring: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Grok, Mistral, Bedrock and more
  • Multi-agent monitoring: CrewAI, LangChain/LangGraph, AutoGen, n8n
  • MCP Server: let an AI assistant query and act on WhiteBoxXAI

Reference

  • Plans & Limits and Governance Events
  • SDK & API and the REST API reference
  • Troubleshooting and the FAQ

docs.title: Quick troubleshooting
docs.text:
AuthenticationError or 401. The key is missing, mistyped or revoked. Check that WHITEBOX_API_KEY is set in the same shell that runs your code, and create a new key if needed.

429 with QuotaExceeded. Your Free plan's monthly Governance Events are used up. See Governance Events.

403 when registering a model. All of your plan's Governed AI Systems are in use. Archive one you no longer govern, or register a new version of an existing system instead.

422 when registering a model. Check that model_type is one of xgboost, random_forest, neural_network, linear_model, llm or custom, and that version, features and baseline_metrics are present.

Predictions don't appear. Make sure you're looking at the model id you logged to, and call client.predictions.get_recent(model_id) to confirm they arrived. If you enabled offline mode, the SDK may still be holding them in its local queue. See Offline Mode.

Lost your authenticator. Sign in with one of your backup codes. See Two-Factor Authentication.

Still stuck? Email support@whiteboxxai.com or use Support in the dashboard sidebar.

docs.title: Governance Events & Governed AI Systems
docs.text:
WhiteBoxXAI plans are sized in two units: how many AI systems you govern, and how much AI activity is recorded. Neither is "API calls". Reading data, configuring things, generating reports and using the dashboard cost nothing. Only recording new AI activity is counted, and the rules are set per endpoint so a batch or an agent run doesn't cost more than the activity it records.

For plan allowances, see Plans & Limits.

docs.title: What is one Governance Event
docs.text:
A Governance Event is one unit of AI activity that WhiteBoxXAI records:

Activity SDK call Events Logged prediction client.predictions.log 1 LLM interaction client.llm.log_call 1 LLM call recorded through a gateway (LiteLLM, OpenTelemetry, Portkey, Kong, Azure APIM) none: the gateway sends it 1 per call stored RAG retrieval client.rag.log_retrieval 1 Safety scan client.safety.analyze 1 Explanation (SHAP, LIME, DiCE) client.explanations.generate / generate_async 1 LLM explanation (attention, token importance, sensitivity, counterfactuals, prompt debugging) client.llm_xai.* 1 Several analyses of one LLM log in a single batch-analyze request client.llm_xai.batch_analyze 1 Bias (fairness) audit client.fairness.audit 1 Drift check or drift report client.drift.detect / create_report 1 RAG evaluation client.rag.create_evaluation 1 Prompt evaluation run POST /api/v1/evaluations/prompt 1 Multi-agent workflow client.agent_workflows.create_and_start 1 per workflow

docs.title: Batches: one event per record
docs.text: Batch endpoints cost one event per record in the batch: predictions.log_batch, llm.log_calls_batch, safety.analyze_batch and explanations.generate_bulk. Batching is neither a discount nor a penalty. It costs exactly what sending the records one at a time would.

docs.title: LLM gateway calls
docs.text:
A call recorded through a LiteLLM gateway or one of the other LLM gateways is one event, the same as a call you log with the SDK. What is counted is what was stored, not what LiteLLM sent: a batch that LiteLLM re-sends is recognised and costs nothing the second time, and a record WhiteBoxXAI cannot read is rejected and costs nothing. A gateway's calls are not grouped by X-WhiteBox-Run-Id; each is its own event.

On the Free plan, a batch larger than what is left of the month is refused whole with 429. LiteLLM does not resend a refused batch, so those calls are lost; the gateway pane counts them and says so. Portkey does not resend either. For the other gateways, check whether yours does; see Limits.

For OpenTelemetry and Portkey, each GenAI span stored is one event. Spans that are not GenAI calls, such as HTTP or database spans in the same export, are dropped and cost nothing, as does a request that cannot be read at all.

docs.title: Agent workflows: one event per workflow
docs.text: A multi-agent workflow costs one event when it's created. Registering its agents, recording tasks, executions and agent-to-agent interactions, and completing it are free, however many there are.

docs.title: Grouped runs: one event per 100 records
docs.text:
Predictions, LLM interactions, RAG retrievals and safety scans that belong to the same end-to-end AI run can share events. Send them with the same X-WhiteBox-Run-Id request header, and every 100 records with that run id cost one event. A 12-call agent run is one event; a 250-record run is three.

The run id is an opaque value you choose: up to 128 characters of letters, digits, ., _, : or -. A header that doesn't match that shape is ignored, and those records are counted individually. Explanations and evaluations are not groupable; each one is its own event.

In the Python SDK, wrap the run in governance_run() and the header is added for you:

import os

from whiteboxxai import WhiteBoxXAI, governance_run

client = WhiteBoxXAI(api_key=os.environ["WHITEBOX_API_KEY"])

with governance_run() as run_id:          # or governance_run("ticket-4821") to choose the id
    client.llm.log_call(
        provider="anthropic",
        model_name="claude-sonnet-4-5",
        prompt=prompt,
        completion=answer,
        latency_ms=812.0,
        prompt_tokens=412,
        completion_tokens=96,
    )
    client.safety.analyze(content=answer, content_type="completion")

Every SDK request made inside the block carries the same run id. Pass your own id to group records sent from several processes.

You don't need governance_run() when:

  • you use the LangChain callback handler: it groups each root chain run automatically
  • you log a multi-agent workflow (CrewAI, LangChain agents and others): the whole workflow is already one event

Over plain HTTP, set the header yourself:

curl -X POST https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/llm/logs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY" \
  -H "X-WhiteBox-Run-Id: ticket-4821" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"provider": "openai", "model_name": "gpt-4o", "prompt": "...", "latency_ms": 640}'

docs.title: What is free
docs.text:
None of these count as Governance Events:

  • Everything you do in the dashboard. Only requests authenticated with an API key (SDK, REST API, MCP server) are metered.
  • Registering, updating, archiving and restoring models
  • Configuration: drift settings, explanation settings, safety thresholds, alert rules, notification channels, trust score weights, brand profiles
  • Alerts, review boards, review requests, the risk register, and compliance evidence
  • Generating, scheduling, sharing and downloading reports
  • Every GET request, and query-style POST requests that read existing records (for example predictions/query, llm/logs/query, explanations/compare, evaluations/prompt/compare)
  • Performance metrics and metric calculators (client.metrics.*)
  • Authoring golden datasets, prompt templates and prompt versions
  • Requests the API rejects. Events are only counted for successful responses.

docs.title: What is one Governed AI System
docs.text:
A Governed AI System is counted by model name:

  • Every version of a model is the same system. Registering credit_scoring version 2.1.0 when credit_scoring 2.0.0 exists never counts as a new system.
  • Archived models don't count.
  • Sample-data models loaded from Settings → Sample data & tour don't count.

When all of your plan's systems are in use, registering a model under a new name (or restoring an archived one) is refused with 403 Forbidden:

{
  "error": "HTTPException",
  "detail": "Your plan includes 1 Governed AI System, and all are in use. Archive one you no longer govern, or contact us to govern more.",
  "status_code": 403
}

To free a slot, archive a system you no longer govern: open it in the Model Register, go to System settings → Archive, or call client.models.archive(model_id). Archived systems keep their history and can be restored later.

docs.title: Free plan: 429 QuotaExceeded
docs.text:
The Free plan's 2,500 events per month is a hard cap. A request that would record new activity once the allowance is used is refused:

{
  "error": "QuotaExceeded",
  "detail": "This organization has used its 2,500 Governance Events for the month. Upgrade to Business Cloud to keep recording.",
  "status_code": 429
}

A batch larger than what's left is refused whole, so nothing is half-recorded:

{
  "error": "QuotaExceeded",
  "detail": "This request would record 500 Governance Events, but only 20 of this month's 2,500 remain. Send fewer records, or upgrade to Business Cloud.",
  "status_code": 429
}

Everything already recorded stays available, and free activity keeps working. Recording resumes at the start of the next month.

docs.title: Business Cloud: billed as overage
docs.text: Business Cloud is never blocked for usage. Events past the 100,000 included each month are recorded normally and billed at $5 per 10,000.

docs.title: Rate limits are different
docs.text: A 429 with "error": "RateLimitExceeded" is the per-client rate limit (100 requests per 60 seconds by default), not your monthly allowance. It comes with X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset and Retry-After headers. Wait for Retry-After and try again. The Python SDK raises RateLimitError with the server's message for both kinds of 429.

docs.title: See your usage
docs.text: Settings → Subscription & usage shows how many Governance Events your organization has used this month out of its allowance. On Business Cloud, usage past the allowance is shown as billed as overage.

docs.title: Plans & Limits
docs.text:
Every plan gets the same governance features: explainability, drift, bias audits, LLM and agent monitoring, the risk register, review boards, and evidence for all five frameworks (ISO/IEC 42001, GDPR, CCPA, the EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF). What changes between plans is how many AI systems you govern, how much activity is recorded, where the platform runs, and what support you get.

Plans are sold in two units:

  • Governed AI System: a model, LLM app or agent system you register, counted by name.
  • Governance Event: one unit of recorded AI activity, such as a logged prediction, an LLM interaction or a bias audit. Configuration, reports, alerts, dashboard use and every read are free. See Governance Events for the exact counting rules.

docs.title: Plan comparison
docs.text: Free Business Cloud Enterprise Edition Price $0, no credit card $599/month, or $5,990/year (2 months free) Lifetime license plus yearly maintenance & support Who it's for Developers, ML engineers and risk leads evaluating WhiteBoxXAI Teams governing AI systems in production Organizations that need full data sovereignty Governed AI Systems 1 Up to 10 (contact us for more) Unlimited Governance Events included 2,500 / month 100,000 / month Negotiated Beyond the allowance Recording pauses until next month $5 per 10,000 events, billed monthly Volume pricing Where it runs Shared WhiteBoxXAI cloud Your own dedicated tenant at <your-org>.app.whiteboxxai.com Your VPC, cloud, data center or air-gapped network Compliance frameworks All five All five All five Explainability, drift & bias ✓ ✓ ✓ LLM, RAG, agent & prompt governance ✓ ✓ ✓ MCP server & agent skills ✓ ✓ ✓ Model-diff architecture reviews — ✓ ✓ Access & audit Role-based access, audit log, Google or Microsoft sign-in Same, plus Microsoft Entra ID single sign-on Runs inside your own identity, key and network boundary Support Community & documentation Standard support, business-day response 24/7 support & custom SLA

docs.title: Free
docs.text:
A lifetime free account for governing your first AI system, with full hands-on access: the REST API, Python SDK and MCP server, explainability, drift and bias audits, LLM and RAG monitoring, safety scans, prompt evaluations, the risk register, review boards and evidence for all five frameworks.

  • 1 Governed AI System. New versions of that system don't count against the limit.
  • 2,500 Governance Events per month, as a hard cap. When the month's allowance is used, requests that would record new activity are refused with a 429 QuotaExceeded response until the next month. Everything already recorded stays visible, and the dashboard, reports and reads keep working.

Sign up at whiteboxxai.com. Only your name, email and a password are needed, or you can sign in with Google or Microsoft.

docs.title: Business Cloud
docs.text:
$599/month, or $5,990/year. Your organization gets its own dedicated WhiteBoxXAI tenant, hosted in Microsoft Azure, at its own subdomain (<your-org>.app.whiteboxxai.com). Your data is stored and processed separately from every other customer's.

  • Up to 10 Governed AI Systems. Contact us if you need more.
  • 100,000 Governance Events per month. Past that, recording is not blocked: extra events are billed at $5 per 10,000, monthly. A production monitoring pipeline shouldn't stop logging because it had a busy month.
  • Model-diff architecture reviews that compare model versions and the code changes between them. See GitHub Diff Reviews.
  • Single sign-on with Microsoft Entra ID, with an option to require it for everyone except break-glass administrators. See Single Sign-On.
  • Standard support, with a response within one business day.

Business Cloud is available now. Contact us and we'll set up your dedicated tenant with you.

docs.title: Enterprise Edition
docs.text:
WhiteBoxXAI deployed on your own infrastructure: your VPC, cloud account, data center or an air-gapped network. Your data, keys and network controls never leave your boundary. It's priced as a lifetime license, plus yearly maintenance and support where you need it.

  • Unlimited Governed AI Systems, with negotiated event volumes
  • Everything in Business Cloud
  • Sized for your workloads
  • Professional installation, 24/7 support and hands-on training

Request a demo to discuss an Enterprise Edition deployment.

docs.title: Demo accounts
docs.text:
A read-only demo account, preloaded with sample models, predictions, drift events, bias audits and reports, is available on request from the pricing page. Nothing can be created or changed in a demo account, and its usage isn't metered.

You can also load the same kind of sample data into your own account from Settings → Sample data & tour. Sample-data models don't count as Governed AI Systems.

docs.title: How long data is kept
docs.text:
Raw telemetry (logged predictions, metrics and LLM call logs) is kept for a set period and then purged. The period depends on the plan:

Free Business Cloud Raw telemetry 90 days, fixed 365 days by default; an administrator can set it anywhere from 1 to 7 years (365 to 2,555 days), per AI system or for the whole organization

Demo accounts aren't purged. Calls older than 30 days are compressed in storage, which doesn't remove them.

The records an auditor relies on aren't part of that purge. Audit-trail events, evidence packs, drift reports and bias audits are kept. When a purge removes the predictions behind an older drift report or bias audit, that report stays and is marked: "Source predictions aged out under retention policy; metrics are locked and cannot be recomputed." Each purge is itself written to the audit trail.

docs.title: Check your usage
docs.text: Settings → Subscription & usage shows your plan, its status and renewal date, and how many Governance Events you've used this month out of your allowance. On Business Cloud, usage past the allowance is shown as billed as overage rather than refused.

docs.title: Need help choosing?
docs.text: Email support@whiteboxxai.com and we'll help you find the right plan, including more systems, a dedicated tenant, or a self-hosted deployment.

docs.title: What does WhiteBoxXAI do?
docs.text: It turns how your AI systems actually behave into evidence a compliance team can use. It monitors models, LLM applications and agents; computes drift, explanations and fairness audits from real data; tracks risks, review decisions and control evidence; and produces reports for auditors, regulators and boards. Every number has a How was this computed? note saying where it came from.

docs.title: What doesn't it do?
docs.text:
• It doesn't certify compliance. It records evidence and shows gaps; your organization, auditor or regulator decides what the evidence proves.
  • It doesn't call your models or LLM providers to generate scores. Evaluations are deterministic checks of outputs you've logged, and nothing uses another model as a judge.
  • It doesn't invent numbers. With too little data, it says a result can't be computed yet.
  • It doesn't cover frameworks beyond five: ISO/IEC 42001, the EU AI Act, GDPR, CCPA and NIST AI RMF.

docs.title: Who is it for?
docs.text: Compliance, risk and governance teams who need defensible evidence about AI systems, and the data scientists and engineers who run those systems. The dashboard's lenses present the same evidence for a compliance officer, a data scientist, an executive or an auditor.

docs.title: Is it cloud or on-premise?
docs.text: Both. Free runs on the shared WhiteBoxXAI cloud at whiteboxxai.com. Business Cloud is your own dedicated tenant in Microsoft Azure at <your-org>.app.whiteboxxai.com. Enterprise Edition runs on your own infrastructure, including air-gapped networks. See Plans & Limits.

docs.title: How much does it cost?
docs.text: Free is $0. Business Cloud is $599/month or $5,990/year. Enterprise Edition is a lifetime license with yearly maintenance and support. Every plan has the same governance features. See Plans & Limits.

docs.title: What's a Governance Event?
docs.text: One unit of recorded AI activity: a logged prediction, an LLM call, a RAG retrieval, a safety scan, an explanation, a fairness audit, a drift check or report, or an evaluation run. A multi-agent workflow is one event in total. Dashboard use, reads, configuration and reports are free. See Governance Events.

docs.title: What's a Governed AI System?
docs.text: A model, LLM app or agent system you register, counted by name. New versions don't count, and archived and sample-data systems don't either. Free includes 1, Business Cloud up to 10, Enterprise Edition unlimited.

docs.title: What happens when I reach my limit?
docs.text: On Free, recording pauses with 429 QuotaExceeded until next month; everything else keeps working. On Business Cloud, recording continues and extra events are billed at $5 per 10,000. Registering a system beyond your plan's limit returns 403.

docs.title: Is there a free trial?
docs.text: The Free plan never expires and needs no credit card. Demo accounts with sample data are also available on request, and you can load sample data into your own account from Settings → Sample data & tour.

docs.title: How do I upgrade?
docs.text: Settings → Subscription & usage, or contact us to set up Business Cloud or Enterprise Edition.

docs.title: How do I sign up?
docs.text: At whiteboxxai.com, with Google, Microsoft, or your name, email and a password. No company details are needed. See Getting Started.

docs.title: I forgot my password
docs.text: Choose Forgot password on the sign-in page and follow the emailed link.

docs.title: Should I turn on two-factor authentication?
docs.text: Yes. It protects the account that holds your compliance evidence, and you need it to vote on governance review requests. See Two-Factor Authentication.

docs.title: Does WhiteBoxXAI support single sign-on?
docs.text: You can sign in with Google or Microsoft accounts. SAML single sign-on and SCIM user provisioning aren't available. Enterprise Edition runs inside your own identity boundary.

docs.title: How do I invite colleagues and set roles?
docs.text: Settings → Users & roles → Invite user, with the role Administrator, Analyst or Viewer. See Settings.

docs.title: How do API keys work?
docs.text: Administrators create them in Settings → API keys. A key is shown once, can be given an expiry, and acts with the permissions of the administrator who created it. See API Keys.

docs.title: How do I delete my account or export my data?
docs.text: Settings → Data & privacy: Download my data (JSON) or Delete my account.

docs.title: What data should I log?
docs.text: The inputs a model used and the outputs it returned. Don't log names, addresses or government ids; put a non-identifying reference in metadata if you need to trace a decision. The SDK's privacy helpers can mask personal data first.

docs.title: Who can see my data?
docs.text: Only users in your organization, according to their role. A request for another organization's record returns 404, exactly as if it didn't exist. Business Cloud runs in a dedicated tenant, and Enterprise Edition in your own environment.

docs.title: Is data encrypted?
docs.text: Yes, in transit (TLS) and at rest.

docs.title: Do I have to log every prediction?
docs.text: No. For high-volume models, log a representative sample with ModelMonitor(sampling_rate=...). Drift and fairness results are computed from what you log, so sample consistently.

docs.title: Can I add actual outcomes to predictions later?
docs.text: Not through an update to the logged prediction. Fairness audits take the true outcomes as input when you run them, and performance metrics you compute yourself can be reported with client.metrics.create.

docs.title: Which models can I monitor?
docs.text: Anything you can call from Python, plus anything that can call a REST API. There are ready-made integrations for scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, PyTorch, TensorFlow/Keras, Hugging Face Transformers, LangChain/LangGraph and CrewAI. See Python SDK.

docs.title: Which LLM providers are supported?
docs.text: All of them. LLM calls are logged with a free-text provider, so OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, xAI Grok, Mistral, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Cohere, open models and local models all work. Cost is calculated for model names WhiteBoxXAI has prices for (current OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Azure OpenAI models) and left blank otherwise. See LLM monitoring.

docs.title: Is there an SDK for languages other than Python?
docs.text: No. Use the REST API from any language, or the MCP server from AI assistants.

docs.title: Can an AI agent use WhiteBoxXAI?
docs.text: Yes, through the MCP server (197 tools) or the SDK. Give it the agent skills, which tell it to report results honestly and never vote on a person's behalf.

docs.title: Which explanation methods are there?
docs.text: SHAP (kernel and tree), LIME (tabular) and DiCE counterfactuals. Explanations run the model itself, so the model file must be stored with WhiteBoxXAI through GitHub registration with storage_mode: full. See Assurance.

docs.title: How is drift detected?
docs.text: Each feature in a recent window of predictions is compared with the baseline: Kolmogorov–Smirnov and PSI for continuous features, chi-squared and Jensen–Shannon divergence for categorical ones, plus concept-drift methods. Sensitivity presets set the thresholds. See Drift Detection.

docs.title: What does a fairness audit need?
docs.text: True outcomes, predicted outcomes, and the group each record belongs to, which you supply. WhiteBoxXAI doesn't infer protected attributes. See Assurance → Fairness.

docs.title: Are LLM answers checked for safety?
docs.text: Yes, if you send them to client.safety.analyze: toxicity categories, 12 types of personal data, and harmful content. Jailbreak and prompt-injection detection aren't part of WhiteBoxXAI.

docs.title: When do alert rules fire?
docs.text: When metrics are logged, drift reports are created or bias audits complete, active rules for that model are evaluated, and any rule whose conditions are met opens an alert in Needs Attention. See When rules are evaluated.

docs.title: Which notification channels are there?
docs.text: Slack, email, webhook, SMS and PagerDuty, set up by an administrator in Settings → Integrations.

docs.title: What reports can I generate?
docs.text: Twelve report types, including a Quarterly Board Pack, an ISO/IEC 42001 Statement of Applicability, EU AI Act Annex IV documentation, a GDPR DPIA record, a CCPA ADMT risk assessment, a NIST AI RMF profile, model cards, fairness and drift reports, evidence packs and an auditor traceability matrix, as PDF, Word or HTML. See Reports.

docs.title: How do I give a report to an external auditor?
docs.text: Share with an auditor sends a link that only works after the recipient verifies a code sent to their email. Links expire, carry a watermark, and can be revoked. See Share a report with an auditor.

docs.title: Can I schedule reports?
docs.text: Yes, daily, weekly, every 30 or 90 days, or on a custom schedule. See Reports → Schedules.

docs.title: Can an AI assistant or pipeline approve a model?
docs.text: No. Votes on review requests need a person's own signed-in session, two-factor authentication and a current authenticator code, and are refused if the request changed since they opened it. Organization API keys can't vote. Pipelines can gate deployments on policy instead; see Policy-as-Code & GitOps.

docs.title: Can the person who raised a request approve it?
docs.text: No. Submitters can't vote on their own requests, and that's enforced on every path, including the API.

docs.title: Can a recorded decision be changed?
docs.text: No. The decision archive is immutable. A mistake is corrected by recording a correction that supersedes the original, with both kept. See Reviews & Decisions.

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text: See Troubleshooting for error messages, and Getting support to contact us: Support in the dashboard sidebar, or support@whiteboxxai.com.

docs.title: In the dashboard
docs.text:
Choose Support in the sidebar footer, or search for Help & Support with ⌘K. The Help & Support page links to these docs and has a request form:

Field Options Category Technical Support, New Feature Request, General Feedback, Billing Urgency / Priority Low, Medium, High, Critical Subject and Description / Feedback What happened, what you expected, and the steps to reproduce it

The form attaches a little context automatically, so you don't have to look it up: your organization, the page you were on, your screen size, and whether you use the Enhanced or Classic layout. You can view exactly what will be attached before you send it. Submit Request returns a ticket reference; quote it in any follow-up.

docs.title: Ask a browser AI assistant
docs.text: Browser sidecar assistants, such as Copilot in Microsoft Edge or Gemini in Chrome, can read, summarise and answer questions about the live documentation at docs.whiteboxxai.com while you work. Open the assistant beside a docs page and ask, for example, "How do I share a report with an external auditor?" They read the current pages; they aren't specially trained on WhiteBoxXAI, so check their answers against the page they cite. For AI coding agents, see Agent & Developer Resources.

docs.title: By email
docs.text:
Email support@whiteboxxai.com. Include:

  • your organization name and the email address you sign in with
  • the AI system (model) name or id, if the issue is about one
  • the request id or error message you saw, and roughly when
  • for SDK or API issues: the SDK version (pip show whitebox-xai-sdk), Python version, and the smallest code that reproduces the problem

Never send API keys, passwords, authenticator codes or backup codes. We'll never ask for them.

docs.title: Support by plan
docs.text: Plan Support Free Community and documentation Business Cloud Standard support, with a response within one business day Enterprise Edition 24/7 support and a custom SLA, plus professional installation and training

docs.title: Before you contact us
docs.text:
• Troubleshooting covers the most common errors, including 401, 403, 404, 422 and 429 responses.
  • The FAQ answers questions about plans, data handling and integrations.
  • What's new lists recent changes that may explain different behaviour.

docs.title: Security issues
docs.text: If you believe you've found a security vulnerability in WhiteBoxXAI, email support@whiteboxxai.com with "Security" in the subject line, and don't include sensitive details in public places such as GitHub issues.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Find the error you're seeing, then work through the steps. If you're still stuck, see Getting help.

docs.title: Reading an error
docs.text:
Every API error uses the same envelope, and the SDK raises a matching exception:

{"error": "HTTPException", "detail": "Model not found", "status_code": 404}
Status error SDK exception Usual cause 400 HTTPException APIError The request can't be carried out as sent, for example an invalid YAML policy 401 HTTPException AuthenticationError Missing, mistyped, revoked or expired key 403 HTTPException APIError Role, plan limit, or an action that needs a person's own session 404 HTTPException APIError The id doesn't exist in your organization 409 HTTPException APIError Duplicate name, or the record changed since you loaded it 422 ValidationError ValidationError A field is missing or the wrong type; detail names each one 429 QuotaExceeded or RateLimitExceeded RateLimitError Monthly allowance used up, or too many requests 5xx ServerError A problem on our side; the SDK retries, then raises

Every response has an X-Request-ID header. Include it when you contact support.

docs.title: No module named 'whiteboxxai'
docs.text:
The SDK isn't installed in the environment running your code:

pip install whitebox-xai-sdk
python -c "import whiteboxxai, sys; print(whiteboxxai.__version__, sys.executable)"

The package is whitebox-xai-sdk; the import is whiteboxxai.

docs.title: ValueError about a missing API key, or TypeError: ... 'api_key'
docs.text:
WhiteBoxXAI() reads the key from WHITEBOX_API_KEY (and the address from WHITEBOX_BASE_URL) when you don't pass them. The error means the variable isn't set in the process running your code, so check it there, not only in your shell. You can also pass the key explicitly:

import os
from whiteboxxai import WhiteBoxXAI

client = WhiteBoxXAI(api_key=os.environ["WHITEBOX_API_KEY"])

Older SDK versions needed the key passed in, so upgrade with pip install -U whitebox-xai-sdk if you still see the TypeError. The older names WHITEBOXXAI_API_KEY and WHITEBOXXAI_BASE_URL are also read.

docs.title: ValueError from an integration helper's register_from_model()
docs.text:
The helper couldn't work out the model's feature names, or you passed a model_type the API doesn't accept. Pass features=[...] with the input column names, and use one of xgboost, random_forest, neural_network, linear_model, llm or custom. A task name such as "classification" is kept as metadata and the framework's default type is used. See Python SDK → Framework integrations.

If you hit an AttributeError or a refused registration from one of these helpers, you are on an older SDK than 1.3.0. Upgrade, or register with client.models.register(...) and pass model_id= to the monitor.

docs.title: 401 Unauthorized
docs.text:
• Check the key was copied whole, with no spaces or line breaks. Keys start with wbx_live_.
  • Check WHITEBOX_API_KEY is set in the process that makes the request, not only in your shell.
  • In Settings → API keys, check the key hasn't been revoked or passed its expiry. A key also stops working if the administrator who created it is deactivated.
  • Using a signed-in session token rather than a key? It expires after about 30 minutes. Use an API key for anything unattended.

docs.title: 403 Forbidden
docs.text:
• Your role. Some actions are administrator-only, such as creating API keys, approving evidence, deciding control applicability, or editing boards and scales. Check your role in Settings → Users & roles.
  • Your plan's Governed AI Systems are all in use. Registering a model under a new name, or restoring an archived one, returns "Your plan includes 1 Governed AI System, and all are in use." Archive a system you no longer govern, or register a new version of an existing one. See Governance Events.
  • Model diff on the Free plan. Model-diff reviews are included on Business Cloud and Enterprise Edition.
  • Voting or finalizing a review with an API key. Votes need a person's own session; see Votes are refused.
  • Demo accounts are read-only.

docs.title: 404 Not Found
docs.text: A 404 on an id means the record doesn't exist in your organization: records in other organizations look exactly like records that don't exist. Check you're using the right id and the right API key. Don't retry with other credentials.

docs.title: 429 with QuotaExceeded
docs.text: Your Free plan has used its 2,500 Governance Events for the month, or a batch is larger than what's left (a batch is refused whole). Recording resumes next month; reads, configuration, reports and the dashboard keep working. To use events more slowly, sample high-volume models and group run records with governance_run(). See Governance Events.

docs.title: 429 with RateLimitExceeded
docs.text: Too many requests in the current window (100 per 60 seconds by default). Wait for the number of seconds in Retry-After. The SDK does this for waits of 60 seconds or less. Use batch endpoints for volume.

docs.title: Predictions aren't showing
docs.text:
1. Check the model id you're logging to:

    for m in client.models.list(search="credit"):
    print(m["id"], m["name"], m["version"])
print(client.predictions.get_recent(model_id))

  2. Check sampling. With ModelMonitor(sampling_rate=...) below 1.0, some predictions are skipped on purpose.

  3. Flush buffers. With buffer_size set, call monitor.flush() or use the monitor as a context manager.
