docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
Step-by-step walkthroughs that end with something you could show an auditor or a review board. Each uses real WhiteBoxXAI features and runnable code; none needs data you don't already have, and the first needs no code at all.

Tutorial You'll end up with Time Code? Explore with sample data A populated dashboard, a board presentation and a sample evidence pack 15 min No From model to evidence pack A monitored credit model with drift, explanations, a fairness audit, a review decision and an evidence pack 45 min Python Govern an LLM application An LLM app with logged calls, safety scans, a governed prompt version and a regression check 40 min Python Govern your agents in 5 minutes An assistant connected over MCP that answers from your data and has recorded a first drift report 5 min Config only Connect an AI assistant over MCP An assistant that answers compliance questions from your WhiteBoxXAI data and prepares a review 20 min Config only

New to WhiteBoxXAI? Start with Getting Started, then come back here.

docs.title: Explore with sample data
docs.text: See what WhiteBoxXAI shows an auditor or a board before you connect anything of your own. This takes about 15 minutes and needs no code.

docs.title: 1. Load sample data
docs.text:
1. Sign in, or create a free account.
  2. Go to Settings → Sample data & tour and choose Load sample data.

Sample models, predictions, drift events, bias audits and reports are added to your account. The header shows Demo data — illustrative only while they're loaded, so nobody mistakes them for your own, and sample models don't count against your plan's Governed AI Systems. Reset sample data on the same pane removes them.

docs.title: 2. Take the tour
docs.text: Press ⌘K (or Ctrl+K) and choose Take the product tour. It stops at each section: Overview, Needs Attention, Model Register, Assurance, Observability, Compliance & Evidence, Reviews & Decisions, and search and shortcuts.

docs.title: 3. Read a dossier
docs.text:
1. Open Model Register (g then r) and click a sample system.
  2. Read the four Governance verdict cards, then open How was this computed? on one of them. It names the records and the method behind the verdict.
  3. Look through the Signals tabs: Drift, Fairness, Explainability, Lineage & versions, and the Model card.

Try switching View as between Compliance Officer, Data Scientist and Executive: the columns and wording change, the evidence doesn't.

docs.title: 4. Check readiness for a framework
docs.text:
1. Go to Compliance & Evidence → Frameworks (g then e).
  2. Pick a framework card and read its N of M controls with approved evidence and its open gaps.
  3. Open the framework to see the detail: ISO/IEC 42001 controls by clause, EU AI Act risk classifications, or NIST AI RMF functions.

Readiness is always a count of evidenced controls, never a percentage. See Compliance frameworks for why.

docs.title: 5. Present to a board
docs.text: On Overview, choose Present. Step through Where we stand, Compliance readiness, What changed and Decisions with the arrow keys, then Print to get one slide per page. Press Exit when you're done.

docs.title: 6. Generate an evidence pack
docs.text:
1. Go to Compliance & Evidence → Evidence packs.
  2. Choose The whole organization, PDF, and Generate evidence pack.
  3. Open Reports → History, download it, and try Share with an auditor with your own email address to see the verification-code flow a recipient goes through.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: When you're ready to use your own data, run the readiness setup (Overview → Set up readiness) and follow Getting Started, or work through From model to evidence pack.

docs.title: Tutorial: connect an AI assistant over MCP
docs.text:
You'll give an AI assistant read-and-act access to your WhiteBoxXAI data through the MCP server, and use it the way a risk officer would: where do we stand on ISO 42001, what's firing, what's waiting for review? It takes about 20 minutes and needs no code.

You need: an MCP-capable client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code), a WhiteBoxXAI API key, and Python 3.11 or later for the local server. Some data helps: load sample data if your account is empty.

docs.title: 1. Install and connect
docs.text:
pip install whiteboxxai-mcp

Add the server to your client. For Claude Desktop (claude_desktop_config.json) or Cursor (~/.cursor/mcp.json):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "whiteboxxai": {
      "command": "whiteboxxai-mcp",
      "env": {
        "WHITEBOXXAI_MCP_API_KEY": "wbx_live_..."
      }
    }
  }
}

For Claude Code:

claude mcp add whiteboxxai --env WHITEBOXXAI_MCP_API_KEY=wbx_live_... -- whiteboxxai-mcp

Restart the client. It should list the WhiteBoxXAI tools (197 of them). Other clients are covered on the MCP Server page.

docs.title: 2. Give the assistant its rules
docs.text:
Paste the compliance-assistant prompt into your client's system or project instructions, or tell the assistant:

Read https://whiteboxxai.com/.well-known/skills/whitebox-governance-rules/SKILL.md and
https://whiteboxxai.com/.well-known/skills/whitebox-compliance-evidence/SKILL.md and follow them.

The skills tell the assistant to report empty or unassessed results as they are, never invent a number, and never cast a governance vote. See Agent Skills.

docs.title: 3. Ask compliance questions
docs.text:
Try these, and watch which tools the assistant calls:

Ask Expect "Which AI systems do we govern?" whitebox_models_list, with names, versions and statuses "Where are we on ISO 42001? Lead with the verdict." whitebox_compliance_iso42001_status; in clients that support MCP Apps, an ISO/IEC 42001 status card "What are our open high-severity ISO 42001 gaps?" whitebox_compliance_iso42001_gaps "What's firing right now, and why?" whitebox_alerts_list_instances, then whitebox_alerts_get_triage_context for the top alert "Show me the risk heat map and the top open risks." whitebox_risk_register_portfolio

Check that every number in an answer came from a tool result, and that unassessed controls are called "not yet assessed" rather than given a score.

docs.title: 4. Have it keep a record
docs.text:
Has credit_scoring drifted? Create a drift report so we have a record, and give me its id.

The assistant should call whitebox_drift_detect, then whitebox_drift_create_report, and quote the report id. The report now appears in the system's dossier in the dashboard.

docs.title: 5. Prepare a review, and decide it yourself
docs.text:
What's waiting for review? Summarise the oldest request for me: what changed, what evidence exists,
what's missing, and the evidence snapshot hash.

The assistant uses whitebox_governance_list_review_requests and whitebox_governance_get_review_request. In clients that support MCP Apps, the governance dossier card shows the request with voting buttons.

The vote itself stays with you. Voting needs your own signed-in session on the hosted endpoint, two-factor authentication and an authenticator code, so an assistant running on an API key can't vote. Vote in the card from a personal session, or in Reviews & Decisions in the dashboard. See Governance voting.

docs.title: What you've set up
docs.text:
• An assistant that reads your WhiteBoxXAI data through the MCP Governance Layer
  • Guardrails from the skills: no invented numbers, verdicts with evidence, no automated votes
  • A drift report created on request and visible to everyone in the dashboard

Revoke the API key in Settings → API keys when you're done experimenting.

docs.title: Govern your agents in 5 minutes
docs.text:
You'll connect an AI assistant to WhiteBoxXAI over the MCP server, tell it the rules it must follow, and check that its first answer and its first record come from your data. For the longer version, with compliance questions and a governance review, see Connect an AI assistant over MCP.

You need: an MCP-capable client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code), Python 3.11 or later, and a WhiteBoxXAI API key (administrators create these in Settings → API keys).

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text: pip install whiteboxxai-mcp

docs.title: 2. Connect your client
docs.text:
For Claude Desktop (claude_desktop_config.json) or Cursor (~/.cursor/mcp.json), add:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "whiteboxxai": {
      "command": "whiteboxxai-mcp",
      "env": {
        "WHITEBOXXAI_MCP_API_BASE_URL": "https://api.whiteboxxai.com",
        "WHITEBOXXAI_MCP_API_KEY": "wbx_live_..."
      }
    }
  }
}

For Claude Code:

claude mcp add whiteboxxai \
  --env WHITEBOXXAI_MCP_API_KEY=wbx_live_... \
  -- whiteboxxai-mcp

WHITEBOXXAI_MCP_API_BASE_URL defaults to https://api.whiteboxxai.com. Business Cloud tenants set it to the API address they were given. Restart the client so it starts the server. Other clients are on the MCP Server page.

docs.title: 3. Give the assistant its rules
docs.text:
Tell the assistant:

Read https://whiteboxxai.com/.well-known/skills/whitebox-governance-rules/SKILL.md and
https://whiteboxxai.com/.well-known/skills/whitebox-mcp-server/SKILL.md and follow them.

The rules tell it to report empty or unassessed results as they are, never invent a number, and never cast a governance vote. See Agent Skills.

docs.title: 4. Check that it works
docs.text:
Ask:

Which AI systems do we govern?

The assistant should call whitebox_models_list and answer with the names, versions and statuses it returned. If your account has no systems yet, a correct answer says so; it doesn't make some up. Load sample data if you want something to look at.

Then have it leave a record:

Has the first model on that list drifted? Create a drift report so we have a record, and give me its id.

The assistant should call whitebox_drift_detect, then whitebox_drift_create_report, and quote the report id. Find that report in the dashboard to confirm it exists: that's your check that the assistant reported what it did rather than what it expected to do.

docs.title: What you've set up
docs.text:
• An assistant that reads and records through the MCP Governance Layer, on your API key
  • Rules that keep it from inventing numbers or voting on your behalf
  • A drift report you can open in the dashboard and show to a reviewer

Revoke the API key in Settings → API keys when you're done experimenting. To go further, follow the 20-minute tutorial: compliance questions, alert triage, and preparing a review that a person decides.

docs.title: description: Hands-on tutorial — govern an LLM application with WhiteBoxXAI: log calls from any provider, scan answers for safety, version the prompt, score it against a golden dataset, and check a prompt change for regressions.
Tutorial: govern an LLM application
docs.text:
You'll take a small customer-support assistant and give it the governance a reviewer expects: every call logged, answers scanned for toxicity and personal data, the prompt under version control, and a regression check before a prompt change ships. It takes about 40 minutes.

You need: Python 3.9 or later, a WhiteBoxXAI API key in WHITEBOX_API_KEY, and an API key for any LLM provider. The examples use OpenAI; swap in any provider from LLM monitoring.

pip install whitebox-xai-sdk openai

docs.title: 1. Register the application
docs.text:
import os

from whiteboxxai import WhiteBoxXAI

client = WhiteBoxXAI(api_key=os.environ["WHITEBOX_API_KEY"])

app = client.models.register(
    name="support-assistant-tutorial",
    model_type="llm",
    framework="openai",
    version="1.0.0",
    features=["question"],
    baseline_metrics={},
    tags=["tutorial"],
)

docs.title: 2. Put the prompt under version control
docs.text:
template = client.prompts.create_template(name="support-answer", description="Tutorial prompt")
v1 = client.prompts.create_version(
    template["id"],
    system_message="You are a support assistant. Answer only from the policy text given.",
    user_message_template="Policy:\n{policy}\n\nQuestion: {question}",
    model_name="gpt-4o-mini",
    temperature=0.2,
    version_tag="v1",
)

Open Observability → Evaluations → Prompts: the prompt and its first version are there. Versions can't be edited later; a change is always a new version.

docs.title: 3. Log every call, and scan the answers
docs.text:
import time

from openai import OpenAI
from whiteboxxai import governance_run

llm = OpenAI()
POLICY = "Refunds are available within 30 days of purchase with a receipt."


def answer(question: str) -> str:
    prompt = f"Policy:\n{POLICY}\n\nQuestion: {question}"
    with governance_run():                       # the call and its scan share one event
        start = time.perf_counter()
        r = llm.chat.completions.create(
            model="gpt-4o-mini",
            temperature=0.2,
            messages=[{"role": "system", "content": "You are a support assistant. Answer only from the policy text given."},
                      {"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        )
        text = r.choices[0].message.content
        client.llm.log_call(
            provider="openai", model_name="gpt-4o-mini", prompt=prompt, completion=text,
            latency_ms=(time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000,
            prompt_tokens=r.usage.prompt_tokens, completion_tokens=r.usage.completion_tokens,
            prompt_version_id=v1["id"], model_id=app["id"], session_id="tutorial",
        )
        client.safety.analyze(content=text, content_type="completion", model_id=app["id"])
    return text


for q in ["Can I get a refund after two weeks?", "Can I get a refund without a receipt?"]:
    print(answer(q))

Open Observability → LLM & RAG for the support assistant: the conversation log, token usage, spend and safety results. Each call is linked to prompt version v1.

docs.title: 4. Build a golden dataset
docs.text:
A golden dataset records inputs, the answer you expect, and the answer the model actually gave. WhiteBoxXAI scores what's stored; it never calls your model itself.

In Observability → Evaluations → Golden datasets:

  1. New dataset: name it refund-questions.

  2. Add a row for each case, with the Input, an Expected output and the Stored model output from step 3. For example:

    Input Expected output Stored model output {"question": "Can I get a refund after two weeks?"} {"must_contain": ["30 days"]} {"answer": "<the answer you got>"} {"question": "Can I get a refund without a receipt?"} {"must_contain": ["receipt"]} {"answer": "<the answer you got>"}

docs.title: 5. Score the prompt version
docs.text: Runs → Score a prompt version: choose support-answer · v1, the refund-questions dataset, and Required phrases as how to score. The run reports N of M evaluated rows passed, lists any rows Not evaluated, and records how it was scored.

docs.title: 6. Change the prompt and check for regressions
docs.text:
1. Save a new version, v2, with a different system message, for example a friendlier tone.
  2. Run the questions again with v2 (pass prompt_version_id=v2["id"]) and add the new answers to a copy of the dataset rows.
  3. Score a prompt version for v2 on the same dataset.
  4. Check a prompt change for regressions: baseline run v1, candidate run v2.

The verdict is No regression found, Regression found (with the cases that got worse), or Cannot tell if too few rows were judged in both runs. Only deploy v2 when you're satisfied:

client.prompts.advance_stage(template["id"], v2["id"], target_stage="verify")
client.prompts.deploy(template["id"], v2["id"])     # refused without a passed verification

docs.title: 7. Clean up
docs.text: client.models.archive(app["id"])

docs.title: What you've built
docs.text:
Evidence Where Every LLM call, with tokens, latency and the prompt version that produced it Observability → LLM & RAG Safety scan results for every answer Observability → LLM & RAG → Safety A versioned, immutable prompt history Observability → Evaluations → Prompts Scored evaluation runs and a regression verdict Observability → Evaluations → Runs

Next: Connect an AI assistant over MCP.

docs.title: Tutorial: from model to evidence pack
docs.text:
You'll take a credit-approval model from training to the evidence an auditor asks for: a registered system, logged predictions, a stored drift report, a fairness audit, a recorded review decision, and an evidence pack. It takes about 45 minutes and uses the public German Credit dataset, so you don't need data of your own.

You need: Python 3.9 or later, a WhiteBoxXAI account (the Free plan is enough), and an API key in WHITEBOX_API_KEY.

pip install "whitebox-xai-sdk[sklearn]" pandas

This tutorial records roughly 15 Governance Events and one Governed AI System.

docs.title: 1. Train a model
docs.text:
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.datasets import fetch_openml
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

data = fetch_openml(name="credit-g", version=1, as_frame=True)
X = pd.get_dummies(data.data, drop_first=True).astype(float)
y = (data.target == "good").astype(int)
age = data.data["age"]

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test, age_train, age_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, age, test_size=0.3, random_state=7
)
clf = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200, max_depth=8, random_state=7).fit(X_train, y_train)
accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, clf.predict(X_test))
print(f"Test accuracy: {accuracy:.3f}")

docs.title: 2. Register it
docs.text:
import os

from whiteboxxai import WhiteBoxXAI

client = WhiteBoxXAI(api_key=os.environ["WHITEBOX_API_KEY"])

model = client.models.register(
    name="credit_approval_tutorial",
    model_type="random_forest",
    framework="sklearn",
    version="1.0.0",
    features=list(X.columns),
    target_variable="credit_good",
    baseline_metrics={"accuracy": round(accuracy, 4)},   # measured above, not made up
    description="Tutorial: German Credit approval model",
    tags=["tutorial"],
)
model_id = model["id"]

Open Model Register in the dashboard: the system is there with the accuracy you measured as its baseline.

docs.title: 3. Log predictions
docs.text:
Send the test-set predictions as if they were production traffic. Wrapping them in governance_run() groups every 100 records into one Governance Event:

from whiteboxxai import governance_run

proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]
records = [
    {
        "input_data": row.to_dict(),
        "output_data": {"prediction": int(p >= 0.5), "probability": float(p)},
    }
    for (_, row), p in zip(X_test.iterrows(), proba)
]

with governance_run():
    client.predictions.log_batch(model_id, predictions=records)

print(client.predictions.get_stats(model_id))

docs.title: 4. Check for drift and keep a record
docs.text:
report = client.drift.create_report(model_id, window_size=200)
print(report["id"], report.get("drift_detected"), report.get("drift_score"))

A drift report is stored evidence with an id you can cite. With a short history, the report may say there isn't enough data to judge drift yet. That's an honest answer, not a failure. Open Assurance → Drift for the verdict in plain language and How was this computed?.

docs.title: 5. Audit fairness by age group
docs.text:
A fairness audit needs true outcomes, predicted outcomes and the group each person belongs to. Here the group is age under 25 versus 25 and over:

y_pred = (proba >= 0.5).astype(int)
groups = ["under_25" if a < 25 else "25_and_over" for a in age_test]

audit = client.fairness.audit(
    model_id,
    sensitive_attributes=["age_group"],
    y_true=y_test.tolist(),
    y_pred=y_pred.tolist(),
    group_data={"age_group": groups},
)
print(audit.get("bias_detected"), audit.get("overall_fairness_score"))

Open Assurance → Fairness. If bias was detected with high severity, a draft entry appears in the AI Risk Register for someone to own.

docs.title: 6. Take it through a review
docs.text:
In the dashboard:

  1. Reviews & Decisions → Boards → New board (administrators): create a board, for example "Model Risk Committee", and add at least one other member.
  2. Requests → Raise a review request: type Model deployment, for credit_approval_tutorial. Use Generate AI Template for a first draft if you like, then Save and submit.
  3. Another board member opens the request, reads the evidence, and votes with their authenticator code. You can't vote on a request you raised.
  4. Once quorum and the approval threshold are met, an administrator or the chair chooses Finalize the decision.

The decision goes into the immutable archive under Decisions. See Reviews & Decisions.

docs.title: 7. Generate the evidence pack
docs.text:
types = {t["id"]: t for t in client.reports.list()}
print(types["evidence_pack"])           # check it's ready

export = client.reports.generate(report_type_id="evidence_pack", format="pdf")
print(export["id"])

Or use Compliance & Evidence → Evidence packs. Then, in Reports → History:

  • download the PDF
  • record sign-off as Preparer, and ask a colleague to sign as Reviewer
  • Share with an auditor to send a verified, expiring link

docs.title: 8. Clean up
docs.text:
Archive the tutorial system so it doesn't count against your plan: Model Register → the system → System settings → Archive, or:

client.models.archive(model_id)

docs.title: What you've built
docs.text:
Evidence Where an auditor finds it A registered AI system with a measured baseline Model Register Production predictions The system's dossier A stored drift report Assurance → Drift; the dossier's Drift tab A fairness audit by age group Assurance → Fairness A board decision with votes and justification Reviews & Decisions → Decisions A signed, shareable evidence pack Compliance & Evidence → Reports → History

Next: Govern an LLM application.

docs.title: Python SDK
docs.text:
The whitebox-xai-sdk package is the Python client for WhiteBoxXAI. It wraps the REST API with typed methods, retries transient failures, can queue records while offline, and has drop-in integrations for common ML and LLM frameworks.

  • Package: whitebox-xai-sdk 1.3.0 · Import: whiteboxxai · Python: 3.9 or later · License: MIT
  • Source and examples: github.com/AgentaFlow/whitebox-python-sdk

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install whitebox-xai-sdk

Framework integrations are optional extras:

Extra Adds whitebox-xai-sdk[sklearn] scikit-learn whitebox-xai-sdk[pytorch] PyTorch whitebox-xai-sdk[tensorflow] TensorFlow / Keras whitebox-xai-sdk[xgboost], [lightgbm] XGBoost, LightGBM whitebox-xai-sdk[huggingface] Hugging Face Transformers whitebox-xai-sdk[langchain] LangChain / LangGraph whitebox-xai-sdk[all] All of the above

Check the installed version with python -c "import whiteboxxai; print(whiteboxxai.__version__)".

docs.title: Configure the client
docs.text:
import os

from whiteboxxai import WhiteBoxXAI

client = WhiteBoxXAI(api_key=os.environ["WHITEBOX_API_KEY"])
Parameter Default Purpose api_key WHITEBOX_API_KEY An API key (wbx_live_...). Read from the environment when you leave it out; the older name WHITEBOXXAI_API_KEY also works. base_url https://api.whiteboxxai.com Your API address. Business Cloud tenants use the address they were given. Also read from WHITEBOX_BASE_URL. timeout 30 Request timeout, in seconds max_retries 3 Retries for connection errors, 5xx responses and 429s enable_offline False Queue records locally when the API can't be reached. See Offline Mode.

The client can be used as a context manager (with WhiteBoxXAI(...) as client:, or async with), which closes its connections on exit. Otherwise call client.close().

docs.title: Secure configuration
docs.text:
• Read the key from the environment (WHITEBOX_API_KEY) or a secrets manager. Never hard-code it, commit it, put it in a notebook you share, or log it.
  • Use one key per application or pipeline, so you can revoke one without breaking the rest.
  • Keys act with the permissions of the administrator who created them. See API Keys.

docs.title: What the client exposes
docs.text:
Every method returns plain Python dicts and lists parsed from the API's JSON. Ids are strings (UUIDs). Each method has an async twin prefixed with a, such as client.models.aregister(...).

Resource Use it for Common methods client.models Register and manage AI systems and their versions register, get, list, update, get_versions, get_latest, update_baseline, archive, restore, compare_versions, version_changelog, list_git_versions client.predictions Log and read predictions log, log_batch, get, query, get_recent, get_stats client.explanations SHAP, LIME and DiCE explanations generate, generate_async, generate_bulk, get, get_by_prediction, set_config, compare client.drift Drift checks and reports detect, create_report, get_reports, get_report, get_trend client.fairness Bias audits audit, get_audit, list_audits, get_bias_history client.metrics Performance metrics you report create, create_batch, calculate_classification, calculate_regression, summary, trend, timeseries client.alerts Alert rules and alert instances create, list, evaluate_rule, list_instances, acknowledge, resolve client.alert_intelligence, client.alert_management Alert prioritisation, correlation, root cause, comments, history client.llm LLM call logging and usage log_call, log_calls_batch, query_logs, get_stats, usage_stats, cost_breakdown client.rag RAG retrievals and evaluations log_retrieval, create_evaluation, get_stats, metrics_precision client.safety Toxicity, PII and harmful-content scans analyze, analyze_batch, thresholds client.llm_xai LLM explainability attention, token_importance, prompt_sensitivity, counterfactuals, debug_prompt, batch_analyze; rag_attribution and get_unified_explanation in the next SDK release client.prompts Governed prompt versions create_template, create_version, advance_stage, deploy, rollback, compute_drift client.agent_workflows Multi-agent workflow tracing create_and_start, register_agent, complete, analytics client.risk_register The AI Risk Register list, get, portfolio client.governance Review boards and requests list_boards, list_review_requests, get_review_request, submit_decision client.compliance Framework catalogs and ISO/IEC 42001 readiness list_frameworks, get_framework_controls, iso42001_score, iso42001_gaps client.reports Report types list, preview, generate

docs.title: Register a model
docs.text:
model = client.models.register(
    name="credit_scoring",
    model_type="xgboost",
    framework="xgboost",
    version="1.0.0",
    features=["income", "utilisation", "tenure_months"],
    baseline_metrics={"accuracy": 0.94},
    auto_detect_git=True,
)
model_id = model["id"]
  • model_type is one of xgboost, random_forest, neural_network, linear_model, llm or custom.
  • version, features and baseline_metrics are required by the API. Only pass baseline metrics you actually measured; {} is valid.
  • Registering the same name and version again returns the existing model, so it's safe on every start-up. A new version string creates a new version of the same Governed AI System.
  • auto_detect_git=True records the commit, branch and repository the model came from; require_clean_git=True refuses to record a dirty working tree. See Git context tracking.

Other optional fields include description, target_variable, tags, fairness_attributes and protected_groups.

docs.title: Log predictions
docs.text:
client.predictions.log(
    model_id=model_id,
    input_data={"income": 52000, "utilisation": 0.31, "tenure_months": 18},
    output_data={"prediction": 0, "probability": 0.12},
    latency_ms=4.2,
    metadata={"customer_ref": "c-1042"},
)

client.predictions.log_batch(
    model_id,
    predictions=[{"input_data": {...}, "output_data": {...}}, ...],   # up to 1,000
)

Each record is one Governance Event. Batching costs the same as logging one at a time; group related records into runs to share events.

docs.title: ModelMonitor and decorators
docs.text:
ModelMonitor wraps registration and logging, with sampling and buffering:

from whiteboxxai import ModelMonitor, monitor_model

monitor = ModelMonitor(
    client,
    model_name="credit_scoring",
    sampling_rate=0.1,      # log 10% of predictions
    buffer_size=100,        # send in batches of 100
)
monitor.register_model(
    name="credit_scoring", model_type="xgboost", framework="xgboost", version="1.0.0",
    features=["income", "utilisation", "tenure_months"], baseline_metrics={},
)

@monitor_model(monitor, input_keys=["features"])
def predict(features):
    return model.predict([features])[0]

With buffer_size set, call monitor.flush() before the process exits, or use the monitor as a context manager (with ModelMonitor(...) as monitor:), which flushes for you.

monitor_prediction takes custom extractors when your function's arguments or return value don't map directly onto inputs and outputs:

from whiteboxxai import monitor_prediction

@monitor_prediction(
    monitor,
    input_extractor=lambda args, kwargs: {"features": kwargs["data"]},
    output_extractor=lambda result: result["prediction"],
)
def predict(data):
    return {"prediction": 0.85, "confidence": 0.92}

docs.title: Framework integrations
docs.text:
Import from whiteboxxai.integrations.<module>:

Framework Module Classes scikit-learn sklearn SklearnMonitor, SklearnWrapper XGBoost / LightGBM boosting XGBoostMonitor, LightGBMMonitor PyTorch pytorch TorchMonitor, TorchWrapper TensorFlow / Keras tensorflow KerasMonitor, WhiteBoxXAICallback Hugging Face Transformers transformers TransformersMonitor LangChain langchain LangChainMonitor, WhiteBoxXAICallbackHandler LangGraph and LangChain multi-agent systems none: use client.agent_workflows See LangChain Multi-Agent CrewAI crewai_monitor CrewAIMonitor, monitor_crew 
from whiteboxxai.integrations.sklearn import SklearnMonitor, SklearnWrapper

monitor = SklearnMonitor(client, model=clf)
monitor.register_from_model(
    name="churn", model_type="random_forest", version="2.0.0",
    features=list(X.columns), baseline_metrics={},
)
wrapped = SklearnWrapper(clf, monitor)
wrapped.predict(X_test)        # logged automatically

The helpers' register_from_model() and register_application() send a valid model_type, a version, features and baseline_metrics. Pass features=[...] to give real column names; without them, some helpers fall back to feature_0, feature_1 and so on, and others raise ValueError. If you'd rather control every field, register with client.models.register(...) and pass model_id= to the monitor, as each framework guide shows. These helpers need SDK 1.3.0 or later.

Per-framework guides: TensorFlow, Hugging Face, XGBoost & LightGBM, LangChain, CrewAI.

docs.title: LLM, RAG and agents
docs.text:
client.llm.log_call(
    provider="anthropic",
    model_name="claude-sonnet-4-5",
    prompt=prompt,
    completion=answer,
    latency_ms=910.0,
    prompt_tokens=388,
    completion_tokens=121,
    prompt_version_id=version_id,      # optional: link to a governed prompt version
)
client.safety.analyze(content=answer, content_type="completion")
client.rag.log_retrieval(query=question, results=docs, top_k=5, retrieval_method="vector")

provider is any string, so you can log calls to any LLM provider. See LLM monitoring for provider recipes, and Multi-Agent Monitoring for agent workflows.

docs.title: Group a run: governance_run()
docs.text:
Records from one end-to-end AI run can share Governance Events: every 100 predictions, LLM calls, retrievals or safety scans sent inside governance_run() cost one event.

from whiteboxxai import governance_run

with governance_run() as run_id:            # or governance_run("ticket-4821")
    client.llm.log_call(...)
    client.rag.log_retrieval(...)
    client.safety.analyze(...)

The block sets the X-WhiteBox-Run-Id header on every SDK request made inside it. A run id is up to 128 letters, digits, ., _, : or -; anything else is ignored by the server, and those records are counted individually. The LangChain callback handler groups each root chain run automatically.

docs.title: Explanations
docs.text:
explanation = client.explanations.generate(
    model_id,
    instance={"income": 52000, "utilisation": 0.31, "tenure_months": 18},
    method="shap",          # "shap", "lime" or "dice"; omit for the model's default
    num_features=10,
)

Explanations run your model

SHAP, LIME and DiCE explanations are computed by running the model itself, so WhiteBoxXAI needs the model file. Register the model through GitHub with storage_mode: full; scikit-learn-style pickle and joblib files are supported. For a model registered with metadata only, the explanation is recorded as failed, with a message saying no stored model artifact is available. Drift, fairness audits and reports don't need the model file.

The result is a dict with feature weights and a base value. For counterfactuals, use method="dice" with total_cfs (default 3), desired_class (default "opposite") and features_to_vary (default "all", or a list of feature names).

For many instances, generate_bulk(model_id, instances=[...]) (up to 100) and generate_async(model_id, instance=...) return immediately with ids. Poll get(explanation_id) until its status isn't pending. Set per-model defaults with set_config(model_id, enabled=True, default_method="shap", auto_explain=False).

See Explainability Engine for how values are computed.

docs.title: Drift and fairness
docs.text:
quick = client.drift.detect(model_id, window_size=1000)          # not stored
report = client.drift.create_report(model_id, window_size=1000)  # stored; cite report["id"]
trend = client.drift.get_trend(model_id, days=30)

audit = client.fairness.audit(
    model_id,
    sensitive_attributes=["gender"],
    y_true=y_true,
    y_pred=y_pred,
    group_data={"gender": genders},
)

A fairness audit needs true labels, predicted labels and group membership that you supply; WhiteBoxXAI doesn't infer protected attributes. There's no endpoint for attaching an actual outcome to an earlier prediction, so join outcomes from your own records.

docs.title: Prompt versions
docs.text:
template = client.prompts.create_template(name="support-bot")
v = client.prompts.create_version(
    template["id"],
    user_message_template="Answer the customer: {question}",
    system_message="You are a careful support assistant.",
    model_name="gpt-4o",
    temperature=0.2,
    version_tag="v3",
    commit_hash="9f1c2ab",
)
client.prompts.advance_stage(template["id"], v["id"], target_stage="verify")
client.prompts.deploy(template["id"], v["id"])     # refused without a passed verification
client.prompts.rollback(template["id"], target_version_id=previous_id, reason="tone regression")

Don't pass force=True to deploy to get around a failed verification. See Evaluations & Prompt Versions.

docs.title: Compliance, reports and governance
docs.text:
client.compliance.list_frameworks()                  # keys: iso_42001, eu_ai_act, gdpr, ccpa, nist_ai_rmf
client.compliance.get_framework_controls("iso_42001")
client.compliance.iso42001_gaps(severity_filter="high")

client.reports.list()
report = client.reports.generate(report_type_id="model_card", model_id=model_id, format="pdf")
client.reports.download(report, path="model_card.pdf")   # next SDK release; see below

client.risk_register.portfolio()
client.governance.list_review_requests(status="under_review")
client.governance.get_review_request(request_id)     # includes evidence_snapshot_hash

ExportFormat (PDF, HTML, DOCX, imported with from whiteboxxai import ExportFormat) can be passed as format=, and client.reports.download(report, path=...) saves the file; adownload is the async twin. They are in the current development version of the SDK and aren't in the published 1.3.0 yet. Until they ship, pass format="pdf" and download from /api/v1/export/exports/{export_id}/download. See Reports.

client.governance.submit_decision(...) exists for a person voting from their own session. It needs evidence_snapshot_hash and a current authenticator code (totp_code), and is refused when called with an organization API key. See Reviews & Decisions.

docs.title: Compare model versions
docs.text:
diff = client.models.compare_versions(version1_id, version2_id)
changelog = client.models.version_changelog(version1_id, version2_id)   # markdown
client.models.list_git_versions(model_id)

Available on Business Cloud and Enterprise Edition. See GitHub Diff Reviews.

docs.title: Async
docs.text:
Every resource method has an async twin prefixed with a:

import asyncio
import os

from whiteboxxai import WhiteBoxXAI

async def main():
    async with WhiteBoxXAI(api_key=os.environ["WHITEBOX_API_KEY"]) as client:
        await asyncio.gather(*[
            client.predictions.alog(model_id, input_data=x, output_data=y) for x, y in batch
        ])

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Offline mode
docs.text: With enable_offline=True, records that can't be sent are queued on disk and synced when the API is reachable again. client.get_offline_status() reports the queue, and client.sync_offline_queue() syncs immediately. Records are only counted, and only appear in the dashboard, once they've been delivered. See Offline Mode.

docs.title: Privacy helpers
docs.text:
whiteboxxai.privacy detects and masks common personal data before you log it:

from whiteboxxai.privacy import DataMasker, detect_pii, mask_pii

detect_pii("Contact jane@example.com or 555-123-4567")   # email and phone findings
mask_pii("Contact jane@example.com")                       # "Contact ****************"

masked = DataMasker().mask({"email": "jane@example.com", "amount": 100.0})

Detected types include email addresses, phone numbers, US Social Security numbers, credit card numbers (Luhn-checked) and IP addresses. Masking is a safety net; the better practice is not to log identifiers the model doesn't use.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
All SDK exceptions inherit from whiteboxxai.exceptions.WhiteBoxXAIError:

Exception When AuthenticationError 401: missing, wrong, revoked or expired key ValidationError 422: the request didn't match the API's schema; .fields has details RateLimitError 429: the rate limit or, on the Free plan, the monthly Governance Events allowance; .retry_after is set when the server sent Retry-After APIError Any other 4xx, including 403 and 404 (the id doesn't exist in your organization). Check .status_code; .request_id helps support trace a request. ServerError, APIConnectionError 5xx responses and network failures ConfigurationError, IntegrationError Client misconfiguration, or a framework integration problem

The client retries connection errors, 5xx responses and 429s up to max_retries times with exponential back-off, honouring Retry-After when it's 60 seconds or less. A longer wait is raised straight away as RateLimitError, so your code decides whether to wait.

from whiteboxxai.exceptions import APIError, RateLimitError

try:
    client.predictions.log(model_id=model_id, input_data=x, output_data=y)
except RateLimitError as err:
    print("Throttled or over quota:", err, "retry after", err.retry_after)
except APIError as err:
    if err.status_code == 404:
        print("That model isn't in this organization")
    else:
        raise

A 403 when registering a model means your plan's Governed AI Systems are all in use. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: REST API Reference
docs.text:
Everything in the dashboard and the Python SDK is built on this REST API. Use it from any language. In Python, the SDK is usually simpler: it handles retries, offline queuing and run grouping for you.

Machine-readable contract

This page lists every customer-facing endpoint. A published, machine-readable OpenAPI contract with full request and response schemas is planned. Until then, the SDK's method signatures and the examples on each guide page are the reference for payload fields.

docs.title: Base URL and versioning
docs.text:
https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1

Business Cloud tenants use the API address they were given when the tenant was set up. All endpoints are under /api/v1. Additive changes, such as new fields and new endpoints, happen within v1; clients should ignore response fields they don't recognise.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Send an API key as a bearer token on every request:

curl https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY"
  • Keys look like wbx_live_.... They're created by administrators in Settings → API keys, and act with the permissions of the administrator who created them.
  • A signed-in session token (about 30 minutes) is also accepted, and is required for actions that must be made by a person, such as voting on a review request.
  • A missing, wrong, revoked or expired credential returns 401.

Every response carries an X-Request-ID header. Include it when you contact support.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Errors share one envelope:

{
  "error": "HTTPException",
  "detail": "Model not found",
  "status_code": 404
}
Status error Meaning 400 HTTPException The request was understood but can't be carried out as sent 401 HTTPException Missing or invalid credential 403 HTTPException Not allowed: wrong role, an action that needs a person's own session, or your plan's Governed AI Systems are all in use 404 HTTPException Doesn't exist in your organization. Records in other organizations are indistinguishable from records that don't exist. 409 HTTPException Conflict, such as a duplicate name, or a review request that changed after you opened it 422 ValidationError The body or parameters didn't match the schema; detail lists each problem 429 QuotaExceeded The Free plan's monthly Governance Events are used up, or a batch is larger than what remains 429 RateLimitExceeded Too many requests in the current window; wait for Retry-After 5xx A server error; safe to retry with back-off

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text: The default rate limit is 100 requests per 60 seconds per client. Responses include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset. A 429 RateLimitExceeded response also includes Retry-After, in seconds. Prefer batch endpoints for volume.

docs.title: Metering and run grouping
docs.text:
Requests authenticated with an API key that record AI activity (logging predictions, LLM calls, RAG retrievals and safety scans, generating explanations, running evaluations, starting agent workflows) count as Governance Events. Reads, configuration, reports and dashboard use don't. Events are counted only for successful responses.

Group the records of one AI run with the optional header:

X-WhiteBox-Run-Id: ticket-4821

Up to 128 letters, digits, ., _, : or -. Predictions, LLM calls, RAG retrievals and safety scans sharing a run id cost one event per 100 records. A value in any other format is ignored.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text: List endpoints take skip (offset, default 0) and limit (page size). The maximum limit varies by endpoint and is usually 100 or 1,000. A few newer endpoints use limit and offset. Time-range filters take ISO 8601 timestamps, for example start_time=2026-10-01T00:00:00Z.

docs.title: Common requests
docs.text:
Register a modelLog a predictionLog an LLM callCheck driftGenerate a report 
curl -X POST https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "credit_scoring",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "model_type": "xgboost",
    "model_framework": "xgboost",
    "features": ["income", "utilisation", "tenure_months"],
    "baseline_metrics": {"accuracy": 0.94}
  }'

model_type is one of xgboost, random_forest, neural_network, linear_model, llm, custom.

curl -X POST https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/predictions/log \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model_id": "<model-id>",
    "input_data": {"income": 52000, "utilisation": 0.31, "tenure_months": 18},
    "output_data": {"prediction": 0, "probability": 0.12},
    "latency_ms": 4.2
  }'

curl -X POST https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/llm/logs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-WhiteBox-Run-Id: ticket-4821" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "xai",
    "model_name": "grok-4",
    "prompt": "Summarise this complaint...",
    "completion": "The customer reports...",
    "latency_ms": 712,
    "prompt_tokens": 210,
    "completion_tokens": 64
  }'

# Ad-hoc check, not stored
curl -X POST "https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/drift/detect/<model-id>?window_size=1000" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY"

# Stored drift reports for a model
curl https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/drift/reports/<model-id> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY"

curl -X POST "https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/report-types/model_card/generate?format=pdf&model_id=<model-id>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY"

See Report types reference.

docs.text:
The ingest routes are called by the gateway with a wbx_lgw_ gateway token, not an API key; a token only works for its own gateway type, except that a Portkey token is accepted on the OTLP traces route. docs.title: LLM monitoring (any provider)
docs.text:
WhiteBoxXAI doesn't wrap or proxy your LLM provider. Your application calls the model as it does today, then logs what happened with client.llm.log_call. Because logging is a plain function call, it works with any model you can call from Python:

  • OpenAI and Azure OpenAI
  • Anthropic Claude, directly or through AWS Bedrock or Google Vertex AI
  • Google Gemini
  • xAI Grok
  • Mistral, Cohere and other hosted APIs
  • Meta Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek and other open models on any host
  • Hugging Face, Ollama, vLLM or your own fine-tuned model

The provider field is free text, so use whatever names your team will recognise in the LLM & RAG audit trail.

docs.title: What to log
docs.text:
client.llm.log_call(
    provider="openai",            # required: any string
    model_name="gpt-4o",          # required
    prompt=prompt,                # required
    latency_ms=640.0,             # required
    completion=answer,
    prompt_tokens=412,
    completion_tokens=96,
    status="success",             # or "failure", "timeout", "rate_limited"
    session_id="conv-1842",       # group a conversation
    user_id="agent-7",            # who or what made the call
    environment="production",
    prompt_version_id=version_id, # link to a governed prompt version
    model_id=model_id,            # link to a registered AI system
)

Log what the provider actually returned. Don't estimate token counts; leave fields out when the provider didn't report them.

Cost is calculated from the token counts for model names WhiteBoxXAI has prices for: current and recent OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini and Azure OpenAI models. For other models the call is logged in full and cost is left blank rather than guessed.

Each logged call is one Governance Event. Wrap a multi-step run in governance_run() to share events across up to 100 records.

docs.title: A decorator for any LLM call
docs.text:
Write one small wrapper and reuse it for every provider:

import functools
import os
import time

from whiteboxxai import WhiteBoxXAI

wbx = WhiteBoxXAI(api_key=os.environ["WHITEBOX_API_KEY"])


def governed_llm(provider, model_name, extract):
    """Log every call to the wrapped function. `extract(result)` returns
    (completion_text, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens)."""
    def decorator(fn):
        @functools.wraps(fn)
        def wrapper(prompt, *args, **kwargs):
            start = time.perf_counter()
            try:
                result = fn(prompt, *args, **kwargs)
            except Exception as err:
                wbx.llm.log_call(provider=provider, model_name=model_name, prompt=prompt,
                                 latency_ms=(time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000,
                                 status="failure", error_message=str(err))
                raise
            completion, p_tok, c_tok = extract(result)
            wbx.llm.log_call(provider=provider, model_name=model_name, prompt=prompt,
                             completion=completion, prompt_tokens=p_tok, completion_tokens=c_tok,
                             latency_ms=(time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000)
            return result
        return wrapper
    return decorator

In production, log from a background thread or queue so logging never slows a user-facing response, and consider offline mode so records survive a network blip.

docs.title: Provider recipes
docs.text:
Each recipe shows the provider call and how to pull out the completion and token counts.

OpenAIAnthropic ClaudeGoogle GeminixAI GrokMistralAWS BedrockAzure OpenAILocal (Ollama) 
from openai import OpenAI

openai_client = OpenAI()

@governed_llm("openai", "gpt-4o", lambda r: (
    r.choices[0].message.content, r.usage.prompt_tokens, r.usage.completion_tokens))
def ask(prompt):
    return openai_client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])

import anthropic

claude = anthropic.Anthropic()

@governed_llm("anthropic", "claude-sonnet-4-6", lambda r: (
    r.content[0].text, r.usage.input_tokens, r.usage.output_tokens))
def ask(prompt):
    return claude.messages.create(
        model="claude-sonnet-4-6", max_tokens=1024,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])

from google import genai

gemini = genai.Client()

@governed_llm("google", "gemini-2.5-pro", lambda r: (
    r.text, r.usage_metadata.prompt_token_count, r.usage_metadata.candidates_token_count))
def ask(prompt):
    return gemini.models.generate_content(model="gemini-2.5-pro", contents=prompt)

Grok's API is OpenAI-compatible, so the OpenAI SDK works with xAI's base URL:

import os

from openai import OpenAI

grok = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.x.ai/v1", api_key=os.environ["XAI_API_KEY"])

@governed_llm("xai", "grok-4", lambda r: (
    r.choices[0].message.content, r.usage.prompt_tokens, r.usage.completion_tokens))
def ask(prompt):
    return grok.chat.completions.create(
        model="grok-4", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])

import os

from mistralai import Mistral

mistral = Mistral(api_key=os.environ["MISTRAL_API_KEY"])

@governed_llm("mistral", "mistral-large-latest", lambda r: (
    r.choices[0].message.content, r.usage.prompt_tokens, r.usage.completion_tokens))
def ask(prompt):
    return mistral.chat.complete(
        model="mistral-large-latest", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])

The Bedrock Converse API works the same way for every model Bedrock hosts:

import boto3

bedrock = boto3.client("bedrock-runtime")
MODEL = "anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"   # or a Llama, Mistral, Nova or other Bedrock model id

@governed_llm("bedrock", MODEL, lambda r: (
    r["output"]["message"]["content"][0]["text"],
    r["usage"]["inputTokens"], r["usage"]["outputTokens"]))
def ask(prompt):
    return bedrock.converse(
        modelId=MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": prompt}]}])

import os

from openai import AzureOpenAI

azure = AzureOpenAI(azure_endpoint=os.environ["AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT"],
                    api_key=os.environ["AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY"], api_version="2024-10-21")

@governed_llm("azure", "azure-gpt-4", lambda r: (
    r.choices[0].message.content, r.usage.prompt_tokens, r.usage.completion_tokens))
def ask(prompt):
    return azure.chat.completions.create(
        model="your-deployment-name", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])

import ollama

@governed_llm("ollama", "llama3.1", lambda r: (
    r["message"]["content"], r.get("prompt_eval_count"), r.get("eval_count")))
def ask(prompt):
    return ollama.chat(model="llama3.1", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])

Model ids change often; use the ones your provider currently offers. Provider SDK details are in each provider's own documentation.

docs.title: LangChain and LangGraph
docs.text:
If your application uses LangChain, the callback handler logs every LLM call for you, whichever chat model class you use, and groups each root chain run into shared Governance Events:

from whiteboxxai.integrations.langchain import LangChainMonitor, WhiteBoxXAICallbackHandler

monitor = LangChainMonitor(client, application_name="support-assistant", model_id=app_id)
handler = WhiteBoxXAICallbackHandler(monitor)
chain.invoke({"question": question}, config={"callbacks": [handler]})

See LangChain and LangChain Multi-Agent.

docs.title: Safety scans
docs.text:
Check prompts or completions for toxicity, personal data and harmful content:

result = client.safety.analyze(content=answer, content_type="completion")
print(result["safety_status"])

Toxicity categories, 12 PII types and harmful content are scored, and flagged categories are recorded as found. analyze_batch(contents=[...]) takes up to 100 items. Each scan is a Governance Event.

docs.title: RAG retrievals
docs.text:
client.rag.log_retrieval(
    query=question,
    results=[{"document_id": "kb-17", "rank": 1, "score": 0.83}],
    top_k=5,
    retrieval_method="vector",
    ground_truth_ids=["kb-17"],     # optional: enables precision, recall, MRR and NDCG
    answer=answer,
)

Retrieval quality metrics are only computed when you supply ground-truth document ids. Without them, they're reported as not computed.

docs.title: Group a run
docs.text:
from whiteboxxai import governance_run

with governance_run():
    docs = retrieve(question)
    client.rag.log_retrieval(query=question, results=docs, top_k=5, retrieval_method="vector")
    answer = ask(build_prompt(question, docs))     # the decorated call logs itself
    client.safety.analyze(content=answer.text if hasattr(answer, "text") else str(answer),
                          content_type="completion")

All the records in the block share Governance Events: one per 100 records.

docs.title: LLM explainability
docs.text: client.llm_xai analyses a prompt and completion pair: token_importance, attention, prompt_sensitivity, counterfactuals and debug_prompt, or several at once on a logged call with batch_analyze(llm_log_id, ...). Each response states the method it used; keep that with any number you pass on.

docs.title: RAG attribution and ungrounded claims
docs.text:
To check whether an answer is supported by the chunks that were retrieved for it, send the query, the answer and the chunks:

result = client.llm_xai.rag_attribution(
    query="Can a customer ask us to delete their data?",
    answer=answer_text,
    contexts=[
        {"document_id": "policy-7", "title": "Data retention policy", "text": chunk_1, "chunk_index": 0},
        {"document_id": "faq-12", "title": "Privacy FAQ", "text": chunk_2, "chunk_index": 1},
    ],
    model_id=model_id,          # optional: files the analysis under an AI system
)

for claim in result["ungrounded_claims"]:
    print("No supporting chunk:", claim)
print(result["plain_language_verdict"], result["analysis_method"])

Each chunk needs text; document_id, title, chunk_index and retrieval_score are optional. You can pass llm_log_id or retrieval_log_id instead of the text, to analyse a call you already logged. The result has chunk_attributions (how much each chunk contributed), claim_groundings (each claim and its best supporting chunk), ungrounded_claims, and faithfulness, context_relevance and answer_relevance scores. An ungrounded claim is one no retrieved chunk supports; it isn't proof the claim is false. arag_attribution is the async version.

Every explanation is stored. client.llm_xai.get_unified_explanation(explanation_id) returns it in one shape whatever method made it: model_type (generative_llm or rag_pipeline), explanation_method, plain_language_verdict, measured and attribution_data.

Next SDK release

rag_attribution and get_unified_explanation are in the current development version of the SDK and aren't in the published 1.3.0 yet. Until they ship, call POST /api/v1/llm-xai/rag-attribution and GET /api/v1/llm-xai/explanations/{explanation_id}/unified directly; see the REST API Reference.

The dashboard shows the same analyses in Observability → LLM & RAG.

docs.title: Multi-Agent Workflow Monitoring
docs.text: Comprehensive guide to monitoring multi-agent AI workflows with WhiteBoxXAI.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
WhiteBoxXAI provides built-in observability for multi-agent AI systems including:

  • CrewAI - Agent crews with roles and tasks
  • LangChain - Multi-agent chains and graphs
  • AutoGen - Conversational agent frameworks
  • n8n - Workflow automation with AI agents
  • Custom - Custom multi-agent architectures

Track agent executions, interactions, task completions, costs, and performance bottlenecks across your entire workflow.

One workflow, one Governance Event

Creating a workflow counts as one Governance Event. Registering its agents, recording tasks, executions and interactions, and completing it are free, however many steps the workflow has. Runs appear under Observability → Agents in the dashboard.

docs.text:
• Quick Start
  • Concepts
  • CrewAI Integration
  • REST API
  • Analytics
  • Best Practices
  • Examples

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install whitebox-xai-sdk

docs.title: CrewAI Example
docs.text:
from whiteboxxai.integrations import monitor_crew
from crewai import Agent, Task, Crew, Process

# Define agents
researcher = Agent(
    role="Research Analyst",
    goal="Find accurate information on AI safety",
    backstory="Expert researcher with 10 years experience",
    tools=[search_tool, scrape_tool],
    llm=ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
)

writer = Agent(
    role="Content Writer",
    goal="Write engaging technical content",
    backstory="Professional tech writer",
    tools=[writing_tool],
    llm=ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
)

# Create tasks
research_task = Task(
    description="Research latest AI safety regulations in US and EU",
    expected_output="List of 10+ regulations with summaries",
    agent=researcher
)

writing_task = Task(
    description="Write 1500 word article on AI safety regulations",
    expected_output="Professional article in markdown format",
    agent=writer
)

# Create crew
crew = Crew(
    agents=[researcher, writer],
    tasks=[research_task, writing_task],
    process=Process.sequential
)

# Monitor execution
monitor = monitor_crew(
    crew=crew,
    workflow_name="AI Safety Article Generation",
    api_key="your_api_key",
    metadata={"project": "blog", "topic": "ai_safety"}
)

# Execute crew (automatically monitored)
result = crew.kickoff()

# Complete monitoring and get analytics
summary = monitor.complete_monitoring(
    outputs={"article": result, "word_count": len(result.split())}
)

print(f"Total cost: ${summary['analytics']['metrics']['total_cost']}")
print(f"Total tokens: {summary['analytics']['metrics']['total_tokens']}")

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
A workflow represents a complete multi-agent execution session.

Fields: - id (UUID): Unique workflow identifier - name (string): Workflow name - framework (enum): crewai, langchain, autogen, n8n, custom - status (enum): pending, running, completed, failed, cancelled - inputs (JSON): Workflow inputs - outputs (JSON): Workflow outputs - metadata (JSON): Custom metadata - tags (array): Searchable tags - total_tokens (int): Total tokens consumed - total_cost (float): Total cost in USD - started_at (timestamp): Start time - completed_at (timestamp): End time - duration_ms (int): Duration in milliseconds

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
An agent is an AI entity with a specific role, capabilities, and model.

Fields: - id (UUID): Unique agent identifier - name (string): Agent name - role (string): Agent role (researcher, writer, analyst, etc.) - agent_type (string): Framework-specific type - model_name (string): LLM model name (for example gpt-4o or claude-sonnet-4-6) - llm_provider (string): Provider (openai, anthropic, etc.) - llm_config (JSON): Model configuration - system_prompt (text): Agent system prompt - goal (text): Agent goal - backstory (text): Agent backstory - tools (array): Available tools - capabilities (array): Agent capabilities - total_executions (int): Execution count - total_tokens (int): Tokens consumed - total_cost (float): Cost in USD

docs.title: Execution
docs.text:
An execution represents a single agent run.

Fields: - id (UUID): Unique execution identifier - agent_id (UUID): Associated agent - parent_execution_id (UUID): Parent execution (for hierarchical/delegated runs) - execution_order (int): Sequential order - status (enum): pending, running, completed, failed, cancelled - inputs (JSON): Execution inputs - outputs (JSON): Execution outputs - llm_calls (int): LLM API calls made - tool_calls (int): Tool invocations - tokens_used (int): Tokens consumed - cost (float): Execution cost - started_at (timestamp): Start time - completed_at (timestamp): End time - duration_ms (int): Duration in milliseconds - span_id (string): OpenTelemetry span ID

docs.title: Interaction
docs.text:
An interaction represents agent-to-agent communication.

Interaction Types: - delegation: Agent delegates task to another agent - handoff: Agent passes control to another agent - query: Agent requests information from another agent - feedback: Agent provides feedback to another agent

Fields: - id (UUID): Unique interaction identifier - interaction_type (enum): Type of interaction - from_agent_id (UUID): Source agent - to_agent_id (UUID): Target agent - from_execution_id (UUID): Source execution (optional) - to_execution_id (UUID): Target execution (optional) - message (text): Interaction message - metadata (JSON): Additional context - timestamp (timestamp): Interaction time

docs.title: Task
docs.text:
A task represents a discrete unit of work in the workflow.

Fields: - id (UUID): Unique task identifier - task_name (string): Task name - description (text): Task description - task_type (enum): research, writing, analysis, review, custom - expected_output (text): Expected output description - status (enum): pending, in_progress, completed, failed, cancelled - input_data (JSON): Task inputs - output_data (JSON): Task outputs - context (JSON): Additional context - agent_id (UUID): Assigned agent - parent_task_id (UUID): Parent task (for subtasks) - priority (int): Task priority - retries (int): Retry count - tools_used (array): Tools invoked - assigned_at (timestamp): Assignment time - started_at (timestamp): Start time - completed_at (timestamp): End time - duration_ms (int): Duration in milliseconds

docs.title: Hierarchical Executions
docs.text:
Track parent-child agent executions for delegated tasks:

# Parent execution (agent ids come from register_agent or the workflow's agent list)
parent_exec = client.agent_workflows.create_execution(
    workflow_id,
    agent_id=manager_agent_id,
    inputs={"task": "coordinate_research"},
)

# Child execution (delegated)
child_exec = client.agent_workflows.create_execution(
    workflow_id,
    agent_id=researcher_agent_id,
    inputs={"subtask": "find_sources"},
    parent_execution_id=parent_exec["id"],
)

task = client.agent_workflows.create_task(
    workflow_id,
    task_name="Verify Facts",
    description="Cross-reference all claims",
    task_type="review",
    expected_output="Verified fact list",
    agent_id=reviewer_agent_id,
    priority=1,
    input_data={"claims": claims},
    context={"sources": sources},
)

    task["id"],
    status="completed",

docs.title: Bottleneck Analysis
docs.text:
Identify performance bottlenecks:

bottlenecks = client.agent_workflows.bottlenecks(workflow_id)

print("Slowest Agents:")
for agent in bottlenecks["slowest_agents"]:
    print(f"  {agent['agent_name']}: {agent['avg_duration_ms']/1000:.2f}s")

print("\nSlowest Tasks:")
for task in bottlenecks["slowest_tasks"]:
    print(f"  {task['task_name']}: {task['duration_ms']/1000:.2f}s")

docs.title: Example 1: Multi-Stage Research Pipeline
docs.text:
from whiteboxxai.integrations import CrewAIMonitor
from crewai import Agent, Task, Crew, Process

# Initialize monitor
monitor = CrewAIMonitor(api_key="your_api_key")

# Create agents
researcher = Agent(
    role="Research Analyst",
    goal="Find comprehensive information",
    tools=[search_tool, scrape_tool],
    llm=ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
)

fact_checker = Agent(
    role="Fact Checker",
    goal="Verify accuracy of information",
    tools=[fact_check_tool],
    llm=ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
)

summarizer = Agent(
    role="Summarizer",
    goal="Create concise summaries",
    llm=ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini")
)

# Create tasks
research_task = Task(
    description="Research AI safety regulations in US, EU, UK",
    agent=researcher
)

fact_check_task = Task(
    description="Verify all claims and sources",
    agent=fact_checker
)

summary_task = Task(
    description="Summarize findings in 500 words",
    agent=summarizer
)

# Create crew
crew = Crew(
    agents=[researcher, fact_checker, summarizer],
    tasks=[research_task, fact_check_task, summary_task],
    process=Process.sequential
)

# Monitor execution
workflow_id = monitor.start_monitoring(
    crew=crew,
    workflow_name="AI Safety Research Pipeline",
    metadata={"project": "regulatory_compliance", "deadline": "2026-12-01"}
)

try:
    result = crew.kickoff()

    summary = monitor.complete_monitoring(
        status="completed",
        outputs={"summary": result}
    )

    # Print analytics
    metrics = summary["analytics"]["metrics"]
    print(f"✅ Research pipeline completed")
    print(f"   Total cost: ${metrics['total_cost']:.4f}")
    print(f"   Total tokens: {metrics['total_tokens']}")
    print(f"   Duration: {metrics.get('duration_ms', 0)/1000:.1f}s")

except Exception as e:
    monitor.complete_monitoring(
        status="failed",
        error_message=str(e)
    )
    print(f"❌ Research pipeline failed: {str(e)}")

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Offline mode lets the SDK keep working in environments with unreliable network connectivity. When the API is unreachable, operations are queued in a persistent SQLite database and synchronized once the connection is restored.

Requires SDK 1.0.0 or later (current release: 1.3.0)

Offline mode was not functional before 1.0.0: nothing was ever queued automatically, and sync() failed against methods that didn't exist. If you're on an older version, upgrade — pip install --upgrade whitebox-xai-sdk — before relying on any of this.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Persistent Queue: SQLite-based storage survives application restarts
  • Automatic Fallback: Operations queue themselves on a connection failure — no special code path in your application
  • Auto-Sync: Automatic background synchronization with configurable interval
  • Priority-Based: Operations processed by priority (CRITICAL > HIGH > NORMAL > LOW)
  • Retry Logic: Automatic retry with exponential backoff, and a path back for permanently-failed operations
  • Thread-Safe: Concurrent operation support
  • Resource Limits: Configurable maximum queue size
  • Manual Control: Optional manual sync for fine-grained control

docs.title: What gets queued, and when
docs.text:
With enable_offline=True, these operations fall back to the queue automatically:

  • client.models.register()
  • client.models.update_baseline()
  • client.predictions.log()
  • client.predictions.log_batch()

Only a genuine connection failure triggers the fallback. This distinction matters: if the backend received your request and rejected it — a validation error, an expired credential, a missing model — that raises normally, as it should. Queueing a request the server has already refused would just replay the same rejection later while hiding the error from you now.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
from whiteboxxai import WhiteBoxXAI

# Initialize client with offline mode
client = WhiteBoxXAI(
    api_key="your_api_key",
    enable_offline=True,
    offline_dir="./offline_queue"
)

# Operations are queued automatically when the API is unreachable.
# Auto-sync runs in the background every 60 seconds (default).
client.predictions.log(
    model_id=model_id,
    input_data={"amount": 150.50},
    output_data={"prediction": 0, "probability": 0.92},
)

# Check offline status
status = client.get_offline_status()
print(f"Queue size: {status['queue_size']}")
print(f"Statistics: {status['statistics']}")

client.close()

with WhiteBoxXAI(

) as client:
    # Operations here
    # Auto-sync starts automatically
    # Stops automatically on exit
    pass

docs.title: Client Parameters
docs.text:
client = WhiteBoxXAI(
    api_key="your_api_key",

    # Offline mode settings
    enable_offline=True,                    # Enable offline mode
    offline_dir="./WHITEBOX_offline",       # Queue storage directory (the default)
    offline_max_queue_size=10000,          # Max operations (0 = unlimited)
    offline_auto_sync=True,                # Enable auto-sync
    offline_sync_interval=60,              # Sync interval in seconds
)

docs.title: Parameter Details
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description enable_offline bool False Enable offline mode offline_dir str "./WHITEBOX_offline" Directory for queue database. If you leave it out and an older ./whiteboxxai_offline directory already exists (and ./WHITEBOX_offline does not), that directory is reused so queued records aren't stranded. A path you pass is always used as given. offline_max_queue_size int 10000 Maximum queued operations (0 = unlimited) offline_auto_sync bool True Enable automatic background sync offline_sync_interval int 60 Seconds between sync attempts

docs.title: Operation Types
docs.text:
The offline queue supports five operation types:

from whiteboxxai.offline import OperationType

OperationType.PREDICT          # Prediction logging
OperationType.REGISTER_MODEL   # Model registration
OperationType.UPDATE_BASELINE  # Baseline updates
OperationType.LOG_BATCH        # Batch logging
OperationType.LLM_LOG          # LLM call logging (queued by client.llm.log_call())

client.llm.log_call() queues its record automatically when offline mode is on, like predictions do.

docs.title: Priority Levels
docs.text:
Operations are processed by priority:

from whiteboxxai.offline import OperationPriority

OperationPriority.CRITICAL  # Priority 4 - Processed first
OperationPriority.HIGH      # Priority 3
OperationPriority.NORMAL    # Priority 2 (default)
OperationPriority.LOW       # Priority 1 - Processed last

Within the same priority, operations are processed FIFO (first-in-first-out).

docs.title: Disable Auto-Sync
docs.text:
client = WhiteBoxXAI(
    api_key="your_api_key",
    enable_offline=True,
    offline_auto_sync=False  # Disable auto-sync
)

# Manually trigger sync when needed
result = client.sync_offline_queue(batch_size=100)
print(f"Synced: {result['synced']}")
print(f"Failed: {result['failed']}")
print(f"Pending: {result['pending']}")

docs.title: Batch Processing
docs.text:
# Sync in small batches
result = client.sync_offline_queue(batch_size=10)

# Sync all pending (up to limit)
result = client.sync_offline_queue(batch_size=10000)

docs.title: Get Queue Status
docs.text:
status = client.get_offline_status()
print(status)
# Output:
# {
#     'offline_enabled': True,
#     'queue_size': 42,
#     'statistics': {
#         'total': 100,
#         'pending': 42,
#         'completed': 55,
#         'failed': 3
#     }

docs.title: Cleanup Old Operations
docs.text:
# Remove completed operations older than 7 days
client.cleanup_offline_queue(older_than_days=7)

# Clean up immediately (for testing)
client.cleanup_offline_queue(older_than_days=0)

docs.title: Access Failed Operations
docs.text:
# Get failed operations for investigation
failed_ops = client._offline_manager.queue.get_failed_operations()

for op in failed_ops:
    print(f"Operation {op['id']}: {op['last_error']}")
    print(f"Retry count: {op['retry_count']}")

Queue inspection uses a private attribute

The client's day-to-day offline methods are public — get_offline_status(), sync_offline_queue(), cleanup_offline_queue(). Reaching the queue object itself for inspection or requeueing still goes through client._offline_manager, which is private and may change. You don't need it for normal operation.

docs.title: Automatic Retry
docs.text:
Failed operations are automatically retried with exponential backoff:

  1. First attempt fails → queued for retry
  2. Second attempt fails → queued for retry
  3. Third attempt fails → marked as permanently failed
# Configure max retries (default: 3)
# Set when creating OfflineManager directly
from whiteboxxai.offline import OfflineManager

manager = OfflineManager(
    offline_dir="./queue",
    max_retries=5  # Custom retry limit
)

docs.title: Handling Permanent Failures
docs.text:
An operation that exhausts max_retries is marked failed and won't be retried on its own. Use requeue_failed() to reset those operations back to pending for another attempt — typically after you've fixed whatever was causing them to fail:

queue = client._offline_manager.queue

# Investigate first
for op in queue.get_failed_operations():
    print(f"Failed: {op['operation_type']}")
    print(f"Error: {op['last_error']}")
    print(f"Data: {op['data']}")

# Reset all permanently-failed operations to pending
count = queue.requeue_failed()
print(f"Requeued {count} operations")

# Then sync
client.sync_offline_queue()

Check the error before requeueing

requeue_failed() resets everything that's failed. If the failures were caused by a genuine problem with the data rather than by connectivity, they'll simply fail again — read last_error first.

client = WhiteBoxXAI(
    api_key="your_api_key",
    enable_offline=True,
    offline_dir="/var/lib/whiteboxxai/queue",  # Persistent location
    offline_max_queue_size=100000,            # Large queue
    offline_auto_sync=True,
    offline_sync_interval=30,                 # Frequent sync
)

# Use batch operations when possible

# Minimal connectivity environment
client = WhiteBoxXAI(
    api_key="your_api_key",
    enable_offline=True,
    offline_dir="./local_queue",
    offline_auto_sync=False,  # Manual control
)

# Make predictions offline

try:

except Exception as e:

docs.title: With ModelMonitor
docs.text:
from whiteboxxai import WhiteBoxXAI, ModelMonitor

client = WhiteBoxXAI(
    api_key="your_api_key",
    enable_offline=True
)

# Create monitor for a model you registered earlier
monitor = ModelMonitor(client, model_id=model_id)

# Log a prediction - automatically queued if offline
monitor.log_prediction(
    inputs={"income": 52000, "utilisation": 0.31},
    output={"prediction": 0, "probability": 0.12},

# Predictions queued and synced automatically

docs.title: Batch Prediction Pattern
docs.text:
# Process large batches with offline support
predictions = []

for batch in batches:
    y_pred = model.predict(batch)
    predictions.append(y_pred)

    # Log to WhiteBoxXAI - queued if offline
    try:
        client.predictions.log(
            model_id=model_id,
            input_data=batch,
            output_data=y_pred
        )
    except Exception:
        # Automatically queued in offline mode
        pass

# Check queue after processing
status = client.get_offline_status()
print(f"Queued: {status['queue_size']}")

docs.title: Queue Health Checks
docs.text:
def check_queue_health(client):
    """Monitor queue health."""
    if not client.is_offline_enabled():
        return {"status": "offline_disabled"}

    status = client.get_offline_status()
    stats = status['statistics']

    # Check queue size
    if stats['pending'] > 5000:
        print("WARNING: Large queue size")

    # Check failure rate
    total = stats['total']
    failed = stats['failed']
    if total > 0 and (failed / total) > 0.1:
        print("WARNING: High failure rate")

    return status

# Run periodically
status = check_queue_health(client)

docs.title: Metrics Export
docs.text:
# Export queue metrics for monitoring systems
def get_queue_metrics(client):
    """Get metrics for external monitoring."""
    status = client.get_offline_status()
    stats = status['statistics']

    return {
        'whiteboxxai_queue_size': stats['pending'],
        'whiteboxxai_queue_completed': stats['completed'],
        'whiteboxxai_queue_failed': stats['failed'],
        'whiteboxxai_queue_total': stats['total'],
    }

# Send to monitoring system
metrics = get_queue_metrics(client)
# ... send to Azure Monitor / Application Insights, Prometheus, etc.

docs.title: Queue Database Locked
docs.text:
If you see "database is locked" errors:

# Ensure only one client instance per queue directory
# Or use different offline_dir for each instance

client1 = WhiteBoxXAI(enable_offline=True, offline_dir="./queue1")
client2 = WhiteBoxXAI(enable_offline=True, offline_dir="./queue2")

docs.title: Queue Growing Too Large
docs.text:
# Monitor and limit queue size
status = client.get_offline_status()
if status['queue_size'] > 10000:
    # Clean up old completed operations
    client.cleanup_offline_queue(older_than_days=1)

    # Or reduce queue size limit
    # (requires recreating client with new limit)

docs.title: Sync Not Working
docs.text:
# Check if auto-sync is running
if client._offline_manager._sync_running:
    print("Auto-sync is active")
else:
    print("Auto-sync is stopped")
    # Restart if needed
    client._offline_manager.start_auto_sync()

# Force manual sync
result = client.sync_offline_queue()
print(result)

docs.title: Queue Size Limits
docs.text:
• SQLite performs well up to 100K operations
  • Set offline_max_queue_size based on available disk space
  • Regular cleanup prevents unbounded growth

docs.title: Sync Interval Tuning
docs.text:
• High-frequency (10-30s): Real-time monitoring, good connectivity
  • Medium (60-300s): Standard production use
  • Low-frequency (300+s): Low bandwidth, edge deployments

docs.title: Batch Size
docs.text:
• Larger batches: More efficient, but longer sync time
  • Smaller batches: More responsive, but more overhead
  • Default (100): Good balance for most use cases

docs.title: WhiteBoxXAI Client
docs.text:
client.is_offline_enabled() -> bool
"""Check if offline mode is enabled."""

client.sync_offline_queue(batch_size: int = 100) -> Dict[str, int]
"""Manually sync offline queue."""

client.get_offline_status() -> Dict[str, Any]
"""Get offline queue status and statistics."""

client.cleanup_offline_queue(older_than_days: int = 7)

docs.title: OfflineQueue
docs.text:
You don't normally construct this yourself — the client creates one via OfflineManager. Note that it takes a db_path, not a directory (offline_dir is OfflineManager's parameter).

from whiteboxxai.offline import OfflineQueue

queue = OfflineQueue(
    db_path="./queue/queue.db",
    max_queue_size=10000,
    auto_sync=True,
)

queue.enqueue(operation_type, data, priority) -> int
"""Add operation to queue."""

queue.dequeue(limit=100) -> List[Tuple[int, OperationType, Dict]]
"""Get pending operations."""

queue.mark_success(operation_id: int)
"""Mark operation as completed."""

queue.mark_failure(operation_id: int, error: str, max_retries: int = 3)
"""Mark operation as failed, retry if under limit."""

queue.get_queue_size(status: str = "pending") -> int
"""Count operations in a given state."""

queue.get_statistics() -> Dict[str, int]
"""Get queue statistics."""

queue.get_failed_operations() -> List[Dict]
"""Get permanently failed operations."""

queue.requeue_failed() -> int
"""Reset permanently-failed operations to pending. Returns the count reset."""

queue.clear_completed(older_than_days: int = 7)
"""Remove completed operations older than the cutoff."""

queue.clear_all()
"""Empty the queue entirely."""
