POST|GET /api/v1/governance/review-boards/requests/{request_id}/participants
PATCH|DELETE /api/v1/governance/review-boards/participants/{participant_id}

The whitebox_governance_raci_grid MCP tool exposes the same grid read-only for agent clients.

docs.title: AI-assisted governance
docs.text:
WhiteBoxXAI can help boards work faster and more consistently:

  • Template generation — structured review templates based on the review type, model context, and board type.
  • Best-practice suggestions — recommendations that reference the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 42001, and the EU AI Act.
  • Decision summaries — an executive summary, key concerns, conditions of approval, and searchable keywords, generated automatically when a decision is finalized.

docs.title: Automated periodic reviews
docs.text:
Schedule recurring reviews so high-risk models are re-assessed on a cadence:

POST /api/v1/governance/review-boards/schedules
{
  "board_id": "...",
  "schedule_name": "Quarterly Risk Assessment",
  "cron_expression": "0 9 1 */3 *",
  "review_type": "risk_assessment",
  "ai_agent_enabled": true,
  "target_criteria": { "status": "ACTIVE", "tags": ["high-risk"] }
}

Cron examples

0 9 * * *          Every day at 9 AM
0 9 1 * *          First day of every month
0 14 * * 1         Every Monday at 2 PM
0 9 1 1,4,7,10 *   Quarterly (Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct)

docs.title: Search the decision archive
docs.text:
Every finalized decision is stored and full-text searchable, with faceted filters and CSV export for audits. In the dashboard this is the Decisions tab: search (use quotes for a phrase and -word to exclude), filter by outcome, type, board and date, and Export CSV.

POST /api/v1/governance/review-boards/archive/search
{
  "query": "fraud detection bias",
  "final_decision": "approved",
  "date_from": "2026-01-01",
  "keywords": ["fairness", "bias"],
  "limit": 20
}

You can filter by final decision, request type, date range, and keywords, then export the results for compliance reporting or historical analysis.

Other archive endpoints:

GET  /api/v1/governance/review-boards/archive/recent      # Most recent decisions
GET  /api/v1/governance/review-boards/archive/facets       # Available filter values
GET  /api/v1/governance/review-boards/archive/{decision_id}
POST /api/v1/governance/review-boards/archive/export       # CSV export for audits

docs.title: Corrections
docs.text:
The archive is append-only — see The decision archive is immutable. To correct a decision recorded in error, record a superseding entry rather than editing the original. Both remain in the archive, linked by supersedes_id, with the correction_reason explaining why.

When searching, be aware that a request can therefore have more than one archive entry: the original and any corrections that supersede it.

docs.title: Security & isolation
docs.text:
• All governance data is scoped to your organization — there is no cross-organization access.
  • Separation of duties, vote history, and archive immutability are enforced on every write path, including direct API calls, not only in the dashboard.
  • Votes and finalization need the voter's own session and a current authenticator code.
  • API keys are stored hashed and are never returned in API responses after creation. See API Keys.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
AI templates aren't generating — confirm AI features are enabled for your organization in settings.

Votes aren't counting toward the threshold — check that voters are active board members (not observers), that voting_power is set, and that quorum_required isn't higher than your member count.

A vote is refused with 403 asking for two-factor authentication: turn on two-factor in Settings → Profile & security. Organization API keys can't vote at all.

A vote is refused with 409: the request changed after you opened it. Reload, review the current version, and vote again.

A vote is rejected outright: the voter is the request's own submitter. Separation of duties blocks self-voting, so the request needs a different voter, or a different submitter.

A decision isn't in the archive — the request must be finalized to create an archive entry.

A wrong decision can't be edited — that's intentional. Record a correction that supersedes it instead.

Scheduled reviews aren't running — verify the schedule is active, its next run time has passed, and its target_criteria matches existing models.

docs.title: Model Register
docs.text:
The Model Register is the inventory of every AI system you govern: models, LLM apps and agent systems. It's where an auditor's first question, what AI do you run, and who's accountable for it?, gets its answer. Each row opens the system's dossier.

Press g then r to get here. Register a system adds one from the dashboard; to add one from code, see Getting Started.

docs.title: The register table
docs.text:
Which columns lead depends on your lens. Available columns:

Column Shows Model, Type, Status, Owner, Registered Identity and lifecycle Trust score The system's current Trust Score EU AI Act tier The risk classification recorded for the system Lifecycle stage Where the system is in its lifecycle Open findings Unresolved findings against the system Evidence Whether approved evidence exists Last attested When the system was last attested Drift, Fairness gap Latest drift status and fairness gap Last seen When data last arrived from the system

docs.title: Filters
docs.text: Search by name, plus Risk tier, Lifecycle, Drift, Findings, Evidence (Has approved / Missing evidence), Status (Active, Deprecated, Archived), Owner and Tag. Filters are kept in the page address, so you can share a filtered view by sharing the link. Clear filters resets them.

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text:
• Saved views: save the current filters and columns (how)
  • Columns: choose which columns to show, or Reset to default
  • Export CSV: exports every row that matches your filters, not just the visible page
  • Compare systems, or select rows and Compare N selected: compare systems side by side

docs.title: The dossier
docs.text: Click a system to open its dossier in a slide-over. The page address includes the system, so you can link to a dossier directly.

docs.title: Governance verdict
docs.text: Four verdict cards summarise the system's state in plain language. Each has How was this computed? and, for analysts and administrators, Mark reviewed. Marking a verdict reviewed records who reviewed it and when. It's refused if the underlying figures have changed since the page loaded, so nobody signs off on numbers they didn't see.

docs.title: Assurance timeline
docs.text: Assurance events for the system (audits, drift reports, reviews and decisions) in date order.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
Tab Contents Drift Latest drift results for the system Fairness Latest bias audit, including "Recommended mitigations, as the audit recorded them" Explainability Recent explanations for the system's predictions LLM & agents LLM usage, safety and agent activity for LLM-based systems Lineage & versions Every registered version, with Compare versions and see the code diff Model card The system's model card: card version, publication status and freshness

A model card marked Stale — needs refresh says why under Why this model card is marked stale: a newer source commit was registered, or a newer fairness audit or drift report was recorded, after the card was last updated.

Refresh Model Card updates the card from what WhiteBoxXAI already holds: the model's current version and baseline metrics, its latest drift report, and its latest bias audit results. If the system has no card yet, it creates one. Nothing is re-typed by hand, and the card's freshness updates once the refresh completes. From the API: POST /api/v1/compliance/model-cards/refresh/{model_id}.

docs.title: Findings, coverage and history
docs.text:
• Open findings for the system
  • Control coverage: N of M in-scope controls with evidence (a count, never a percentage)
  • Trust score history, with its three components
  • Audit trail: every recorded action on this system

docs.title: System settings
docs.text:
• Edit details: description, status and tags, then Save changes
  • Archive / Restore: archiving asks "Archive this model?". Archived systems keep their history, stop counting towards your plan's Governed AI Systems, and can be restored later.

docs.title: Versions and code diffs
docs.text: Register a new version of a system by registering it under the same name with a new version string. It stays one Governed AI System. From Lineage & versions, compare two versions to see what changed between them, including the code changes when the versions were registered with Git context. Model-diff architecture reviews are included on Business Cloud and Enterprise Edition. See GitHub Diff Reviews.

docs.title: From code
docs.text:
client.models.list(search="credit", limit=50)
client.models.get(model_id)
client.models.get_versions("credit_scoring")
client.models.list_git_versions(model_id)                 # Git-backed versions
client.models.compare_versions(version1_id, version2_id)  # ids from list_git_versions
client.models.archive(model_id)
client.models.restore(model_id)

See SDK & API.

docs.title: Needs Attention
docs.text: Needs Attention gathers everything that needs a person into one queue, worst first. It has three tabs: Needs Attention, All Alerts and Alert Rules. Press g then a to get here, or click the bell in the header.

docs.title: The queue
docs.text:
The queue combines four sources:

Source Examples Alerts Active alerts on a model's performance, drift or safety Risks Open entries in the AI Risk Register Reviews Review requests waiting for a decision Deadlines Audit dates, regulatory dates and review or risk-treatment due dates from the compliance calendar

docs.title: Filter it
docs.text:
• Source and Severity, each with a count
  • Deadlines due within: 7 to 90 days

Save a filter combination you use often with Saved views. See saved views.

docs.title: Act on a row
docs.text: Depending on what the row is: Acknowledge, Assign to me, Open review, Open risk, Open dossier or Open compliance. Acknowledging and resolving alerts are recorded in the audit trail under your name.

docs.title: All Alerts
docs.text: Every alert for your organization, with Total Alerts, Active, Acknowledged and Resolved counts, a search box, and status and severity filters. Acknowledge and Resolve are on each alert.

docs.title: Alert Rules
docs.text: Alert rules describe the conditions you want to be warned about: a metric, an operator (gt, gte, lt, lte, eq, ne) and a threshold, with a severity. The tab lists each rule's Name, Type, Severity, Status, Conditions, Times Triggered and Created date. Create Alert Rule opens the rule form.

docs.title: When rules are evaluated
docs.text:
Active rules for a model are evaluated automatically whenever new evidence arrives for it:

Event Values a rule can match Performance metrics are logged (client.metrics.create / create_batch) Each metric by its name, for example accuracy A drift report is created drift_score, drifted_features_count, and the report's numeric metrics as drift_<name> A bias audit completes overall_fairness_score, bias_detected (1 or 0), disparate_impact_ratio, demographic_parity_diff

A rule whose conditions are met opens an alert, unless the rule is within its throttle window. New alerts appear in this queue and under All Alerts, are counted on the rule's Times Triggered, and are available through the API and MCP server. Escalation policies route alerts to your notification channels.

A rule's metric_name must match the name the value arrives under. Test a rule before relying on it with client.alerts.evaluate_rule(rule_id, metric_values={...}) or the whitebox_alerts_evaluate_rule MCP tool, which checks it without opening an alert.

Choose thresholds yourself. WhiteBoxXAI doesn't present a default threshold as a regulatory requirement.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: Delivery channels (Slack, email, webhook, SMS and PagerDuty) are set up by an administrator in Settings → Integrations, where each channel has Send test. See Settings.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text: Observability shows how the systems in your register behave at runtime. Its tabs are Performance, LLM & RAG, Agents and Evaluations.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
For classic ML systems:

  • Platform health: Healthy, Degraded or Unhealthy
  • System performance over the selected range (7 days, 30 days, 90 days or 1 year)
  • Baseline Performance Metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score and AUC-ROC, as registered with the model, next to what has been measured since

Performance metrics you report from your own evaluation pipeline (client.metrics.create) appear here too. They don't count as Governance Events.

docs.title: LLM & RAG audit trails
docs.text:
For systems of type LLM, this tab is the audit trail of what your LLM application actually did: every logged call, retrieval and safety scan, searchable after the fact. It's the record you need when someone asks what did the assistant tell that customer, using which prompt version, and was the answer checked?

Panel Shows Usage Requests, tokens and spend for the period Safety Toxicity and PII findings, and how many responses were blocked Retrieval quality Precision and relevance of RAG retrievals, where ground truth was supplied Conversation log Every logged prompt and completion, searchable (Search conversations...) RAG quality trend Retrieval quality over time

Pick a range from 24 hours to 1 year. Export Report downloads the panel data.

docs.title: What the trail contains
docs.text:
Each logged LLM call records the provider, model, prompt, completion, token counts, latency and status as your application reported them, plus the prompt version it used if you pass one. WhiteBoxXAI doesn't estimate token counts. Spend is calculated from the reported tokens for model names it has prices for, and is left blank for the rest. See LLM monitoring for which providers you can log from (any of them).

Safety scans check text for:

  • Toxicity: toxicity, severe toxicity, identity attack, insult, profanity, threat, sexually explicit content, hate speech, violence, self-harm and misinformation
  • Personal data (PII): 12 types, including email addresses and phone numbers
  • Harmful content

Flagged categories are recorded as they were found and are never downgraded after the fact.

Retrieval quality metrics are only computed when you supply ground-truth document ids with a retrieval. Without them, the panel says the metrics haven't been computed.

docs.title: Attribution & explainability
docs.text:
When someone asks why did the assistant say that, and was it grounded in the documents it retrieved?, the LLM & RAG Attribution & Explainability panel answers with a computation you can re-run, not a summary. If you have more than one LLM system, choose a Target System first. The fields start with a sample scenario; replace them with your own text.

Tab What you enter What you get RAG Grounding & Attribution A User Query, the Generated Answer and the retrieved context chunks. Analyze RAG Grounding runs it. An Auditor Verdict in plain language, with the analysis method shown. Sentence-by-Sentence Claim Grounding marks each claim Grounded or Ungrounded Claim, with its supporting chunk and similarity. Context Chunk Attribution Weights show how much each chunk contributed. Token Attribution An Input Prompt and the Model Completion, and a Method: Integrated Gradients (Path Integral), Input × Gradient or Leave-One-Out Perturbation. Compute Token Importance runs it. A verdict on the method used, a heat strip over the tokens, and a table of each token's importance score, labelled Salient Driver or Contextual. Prompt Robustness & Ablation The Prompt for Ablation Testing, and an Ablation Mode: Sentence Ablation (Deterministic), Clause Removal or Character Perturbation. Analyze Sensitivity runs it. A Robustness & Integrity Status: Measured Divergence, or an explicit Unmeasured state.

The panel never fills a gap with an invented number. When a result can't be measured, it says Unmeasured and why. An ungrounded claim is a claim no retrieved chunk supports. It is not proof the claim is false, so treat it as a lead for review.

The same analyses are available from code and the API. See LLM monitoring and the REST API Reference.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
Multi-agent workflow runs from CrewAI, LangChain/LangGraph, AutoGen, n8n or your own framework. Filter by status (Running, Completed, Failed, Pending, Cancelled) and framework (CrewAI, LangChain, AutoGen, n8n, Custom). Open a run to see its agents, tasks, executions, agent-to-agent interactions, cost breakdown, bottlenecks and timeline.

Cost, bottleneck and timeline analytics are computed after a workflow completes, and can take a little while to appear.

Each workflow counts as one Governance Event, however many agents and steps it has. See Multi-Agent Monitoring.

docs.title: Evaluations
docs.text: Prompt evaluations, golden datasets, regression checks and prompt versions have their own page: Evaluations & Prompt Versions.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Overview answers where do our AI systems stand, and what needs a decision first? It opens on Now, with two more tabs: Trends and Value & impact. Its two header buttons are Set up readiness and Present.

docs.title: Readiness setup checklist
docs.text:
Until setup is complete, a card shows Your readiness setup: N of 5 steps done, with Start setup or Continue setup. Each step shows Done, To do or Could not be checked:

  1. Adopt a compliance framework
  2. Set your next audit date
  3. Review your control defaults
  4. Connect your first model
  5. Invite a reviewer

Steps are checked against what's actually recorded. "Connect your first model" is done when real data arrives, not when a box is ticked. Once all five are done the card reads Readiness setup complete, with Review setup. If analysts have proposed changes, the card says how many are waiting for an administrator.

docs.title: Attention band
docs.text: A band across the top says how many items need attention, broken down by severity, with a countdown to the nearest deadline. Review all opens Needs Attention.

docs.title: Posture tiles
docs.text:
Tile What it counts Models monitored AI systems in the register that are being monitored Average trust score The mean Trust Score (out of 100) across systems that have one Needs attention Open items in the Needs Attention queue Controls evidenced Controls with approved evidence, shown as "N of M" for adopted frameworks

Every tile has a How was this computed? popover naming the records it counted.

docs.title: Framework readiness
docs.text: One row per framework: N of M controls evidenced, or Not adopted / Assessment not started. Readiness is always shown as a count of evidenced controls, never as a percentage that could be read as "compliant". Open Compliance & Evidence goes to the detail.

docs.title: Needs a look first
docs.text: The systems most in need of attention, with a link to the Model Register.

docs.title: What changed
docs.text: Changes since a given date: average trust score, findings, decisions, evidence, systems added, exports completed and audit events recorded.

docs.title: Trends
docs.text:
Pick a range (Last 30, 90 or 180 days, or Last year) to see:

  • Average trust score
  • Controls evidenced, by framework
  • Findings opened and closed
  • Drift incidents

Each chart has a table view with the same numbers, for screen readers and for copying into a report.

docs.title: Value & impact
docs.text:
Written for executives and boards: ROI and value, Drift impact and Agentic governance. The Executive lens opens the Overview on this tab.

Business Value & Return on Investment shows Financial & Usage Telemetry (Combined AI Spend, LLM Token Spend, Agentic Workflow Spend and Predictions Logged) next to the return figures. The return figures, such as net ROI and human hours saved, are computed only from assumptions your organization has set. Where nothing is set, the tile says it isn't instrumented and why, rather than showing an estimate. An invented ROI number is the kind of figure a board asks you to defend.

The assumptions are the organization defaults and per-system profiles behind GET and PUT /api/v1/executive-dashboard/value-config:

Level What you set Organization Hourly labor rate (USD), and minutes saved per prediction, per LLM request and per agent workflow run Each AI system Governed business goal, monthly infrastructure cost, target monthly volume, minutes saved per unit, monthly revenue at risk, maximum churn risk, latency SLO and monthly operating cost

The editing dialog, Configure Value & KPI Assumptions, is on the Classic layout's Executive Dashboard (ROI & Value tab). The new layout doesn't have the dialog yet, so use the API or switch layout under Settings → Preferences to change them.

docs.title: Readiness setup wizard
docs.text:
Set up readiness (or the first-run prompt Set up your compliance readiness) opens a five-step wizard: Frameworks → Audit dates → Applicability → Connect the SDK → Invite a reviewer.

What you can do depends on your role:

Role In the wizard Administrator Adopts frameworks, sets audit dates, marks control defaults reviewed (Mark defaults reviewed), confirms or rejects analysts' proposals, and invites a reviewer directly Analyst Proposes framework adoptions and dates. "You propose; an administrator confirms." Viewer Sees progress only

Inviting a reviewer sends an email invitation with the role you choose (Analyst, Viewer or Administrator). The invitee sets their own password from the link.

The first-run prompt appears once per browser for administrators and analysts while setup is unfinished.

docs.title: Presentation mode
docs.text:
Present turns the Overview into full-screen slides for a board or committee meeting:

  1. Where we stand
  2. Compliance readiness
  3. What changed
  4. Decisions
  5. Trends & trajectory: trust score, findings, drift incidents and evidence coverage, week by week

Use the arrow keys, Page Up / Page Down or Space to move between slides, Home and End to jump to the first or last, or 1 to 5 to go straight to a slide. Fullscreen (where your browser allows it) fills the screen, Print produces one slide per page, and Exit or Esc returns to the dashboard. The slides use the same live numbers as the Overview, so what you present matches what an auditor would see.

For a document to circulate rather than present, generate a Quarterly Board Pack from Reports, or use ⌘K → Generate board pack.

docs.title: Report types reference
docs.text:
This page lists every report type the Report Studio can generate, with the id to use from code and the data each one needs. For how to customize, brand, sign off, share and schedule reports, see Reports.

All report types generate as PDF, Word (DOCX) or HTML.

docs.title: Report types
docs.text:
Id Name Scope Needs before it can be generated quarterly_board_pack Quarterly Board Pack Organization At least one active model iso42001_statement_of_applicability ISO/IEC 42001 Statement of Applicability Framework: ISO/IEC 42001 ISO/IEC 42001 applicability decisions eu_ai_act_annex_iv_technical_documentation EU AI Act Annex IV Technical Documentation One AI system An EU AI Act risk classification of high for that system eu_ai_act_conformity_checklist EU AI Act Conformity Checklist Framework: EU AI Act EU AI Act applicability decisions gdpr_dpia_automated_decision_record GDPR Art. 35 DPIA / Art. 22 Automated-Decision Record Framework: GDPR Article 30 processing records or automated-decision requests ccpa_admt_risk_assessment CCPA ADMT Risk Assessment Framework: CCPA Applicability decisions for the CCPA ADMT controls nist_ai_rmf_profile NIST AI RMF Profile Framework: NIST AI RMF NIST AI RMF applicability decisions model_card Model Card One AI system An authored model card for that system fairness_audit Fairness Audit One AI system At least one bias audit for that system drift_report Drift Report One AI system At least one drift report for that system evidence_pack Evidence Pack Organization At least one active model auditor_traceability_matrix Auditor Traceability Matrix Organization Control applicability decisions for at least one framework

Applicability decisions are made under Compliance & Evidence → Controls (see Compliance & Evidence). When a report type's needs aren't met, it reports Needs data with the specific reason. It never produces a partial document filled with placeholders.

docs.title: Generate from code
docs.text:
Python SDKREST 
types = client.reports.list()
for t in types:
    print(t["id"], t["name"])

html = client.reports.preview(report_type_id="drift_report", model_id=model_id)
export = client.reports.generate(report_type_id="drift_report", model_id=model_id, format="pdf")

# List report types, with availability for your organization
curl https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/report-types \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY"

# Preview as HTML
curl -X POST "https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/report-types/drift_report/preview?model_id=<model-id>"       -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY"

# Generate; the response is an export record with an id
curl -X POST "https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/report-types/drift_report/generate?format=pdf&model_id=<model-id>"       -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY"

format (pdf, docx or html), model_id, brand_profile_id and template_id are query parameters. To override a template's writing style for one run, send the settings as the JSON body.

The generated report is an export: download it from GET /api/v1/export/exports/{export_id}/download, and share or sign it off as described in Reports. In the next SDK release, client.reports.download(result, path="report.pdf") does the download for you; see Reports.

Every type shares the same layout: a document-control table, a findings summary, "What this section shows an auditor" notes and (in HTML and PDF) a contents list. See How every report is laid out.

Pass model_id only for report types scoped to one AI system. Organization- and framework-scoped types ignore it.

docs.title: Generate from an AI assistant
docs.text: An AI assistant generates reports through the Python SDK, using the calls above. The MCP server doesn't have report-generation tools; over MCP, an assistant can create and read drift reports and read the evidence a report draws on. Have the assistant take report type ids from client.reports.list() rather than guessing, and give you the download link and generation date. The compliance-evidence skill covers this.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
You have a deadline: an EU AI Act milestone, an ISO/IEC 42001 audit, a customer's vendor questionnaire, a board meeting. You need a document you can hand over without translating it yourself first. The Report Studio produces it from the evidence WhiteBoxXAI already holds, in PDF, Word or HTML, with your branding, sign-off and a verified way to share it.

It's under Compliance & Evidence → Reports, with three sub-tabs: Report types, History and Schedules.

docs.title: Why you can trust what's in a report
docs.text:
• Every number traces to a computation. Explanations are live SHAP, LIME or DiCE output, and fairness and drift sections come from recorded audits and reports you can open by id.
  • Nothing is templated filler. A report type that lacks the data it needs says Needs data, with the reason, rather than generating a document with placeholder text.
  • Governance records are enforced, not asserted. Approvals, votes, control decisions and justifications in a report are the ones recorded in the platform, with who and when.
  • Every issued file can be checked later. Verify a file confirms that a document someone hands back is byte-for-byte the one WhiteBoxXAI generated.

For how SHAP, LIME and fairness metrics are computed, see Assurance and the Feature reference.

docs.title: How every report is laid out
docs.text:
An auditor opens a report with one question: what am I looking at, and how much should I trust it? Every report type shares a layout built to answer that.

  • A document-control table at the front: the report, the organization, the scope, the reporting period (when one applies), when it was generated, the frameworks it references, and a How to read this report note.
  • A findings summary: how many findings sit at each rating (Critical, High, Medium and Low), how many areas have no issues, and how many have data gaps. Narrative findings carry a worded rating, so the severity doesn't rely on colour alone.
  • What this section shows an auditor: a short note at the top of each evidence section, with the requirements it is relevant to, taken from the same control catalogs as your Controls.
  • A numbered contents list with links (and page numbers in PDF) in the HTML and PDF formats, once a report has three or more sections. Word (DOCX) reports don't have one.

Charts appear only where the data exists. Depending on the report, they cover trust score by model, open risks by severity, fairness metric values, drift per check and performance against the baseline. If there isn't enough data to draw one, the report leaves the chart out and says the data is missing; it never draws one from placeholder values.

Two reports go further on provenance. The Auditor Traceability Matrix includes an evidence manifest: each artifact, its SHA-256 hash and where it came from. The Evidence Pack states how its audit events were collected (hash-chained) and pins the exported file's hash, so a file handed back later can be checked with Verify a file.

docs.title: Report types
docs.text: Report type Scope What it contains Quarterly Board Pack Whole organization Trust, risk and compliance posture across every monitored model, in plain governance language, including a High-Risk AI Systems section ISO/IEC 42001 Statement of Applicability ISO/IEC 42001 Every control, your in/out-of-scope decision and justification, and a traceability matrix to the evidence for each in-scope control EU AI Act Annex IV Technical Documentation One AI system The Annex IV technical documentation for a high-risk system: intended purpose, design, data governance and risk management measures EU AI Act Conformity Checklist EU AI Act Your applicability decisions against the Act's conformity requirements, with justifications for anything out of scope GDPR Art. 35 DPIA / Art. 22 Automated-Decision Record GDPR Article 30 processing records and Article 22 automated-decision rights requests, in one accountability record CCPA ADMT Risk Assessment CCPA A risk assessment for automated decision-making technology under CCPA/CPRA NIST AI RMF Profile NIST AI RMF Your applicability decisions mapped to the framework's functions and categories Model Card One AI system Intended use, training data, performance and fairness evaluation results Fairness Audit One AI system The most recent bias audit: fairness scores, per-group comparisons and flagged severity Drift Report One AI system The most recent drift analysis, with the baseline and comparison periods it was measured against Evidence Pack Whole organization or one system Trust, risk and compliance evidence bundled for an auditor Auditor Traceability Matrix Whole organization Every in-scope control across every adopted framework, mapped to the evidence an auditor would check

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Each report type card shows whether it can be generated now:

  • Ready
  • Needs data, with the reason, such as "No bias audit has been run yet for credit_scoring", "No ISO/IEC 42001 applicability decisions are recorded yet", or "credit_scoring is classified limited risk; Annex IV technical documentation applies to high-risk systems"
  • Not available yet

docs.title: Generate a report
docs.text:
1. Choose a report type, and the AI system if its scope is one system.
  2. Choose a format: PDF, Word (DOCX) or HTML.
  3. Click Generate. The report is saved to History.

Customize… opens the template editor, and Saved templates lists your versions of that report type, with Edit and Generate.

docs.title: Templates and writing style
docs.text:
The template editor has a live Preview. A template sets:

  • Template name, Format, Brand profile (or Organization default) and AI system
  • Writing style:
    • Audience: Compliance officer, Data scientist, Board and executives, Auditor or Administrator
    • Tone: Formal or Plain
    • Level of detail: Concise, Standard or Detailed
    • Spelling: US or UK
  • Glossary: replace a platform term with your organization's term (Platform says → Say instead)
  • Sections: include, remove and reorder sections, and Add introduction with placeholders
  • Default template: use this template whenever the report type is generated

Save template keeps it, and Generate produces a report from it.

docs.title: Brand profiles
docs.text:
Reports carry your organization's branding from a brand profile. You can keep several, with one set as the Default. Administrators edit them in Settings → Brand profiles; everyone else can view them. A profile sets:

  • Colours, with a contrast check
  • Font: Inter, Arial, Helvetica, Georgia or Times New Roman
  • Cover layout: Classic, Modern or Minimal
  • Header and footer text, Confidentiality marking and Disclaimer
  • Watermark: None, DRAFT or CONFIDENTIAL
  • Page size: A4 or US Letter
  • Logo

Margin text and the watermark repeat on every page of a PDF.

docs.title: History, sign-off and verification
docs.text: Report history lists every generated report, with Download.

docs.title: Sign-off
docs.text: A report can be signed off in three roles: Preparer, Reviewer and Approver. Use Sign as … on a report. Each person can hold only one role on a given file, so the person who prepared a report can't also approve it. Sign-offs are recorded against that exact file.

docs.title: Verify a file
docs.text: Verify a file checks a document you've been handed against the reports WhiteBoxXAI generated. If the file was altered after it was issued, it won't match.

docs.title: Share a report with an auditor
docs.text:
Sharing a report with someone outside your organization, such as an external auditor or a customer's security team, doesn't mean emailing a PDF or creating them an account.

  1. In History, choose Share with an auditor on a report.

  2. Pick a preset:

    Preset Link expires after Watermark Share with auditor 30 days CONFIDENTIAL Quick preview 2 days DRAFT

  3. Enter the recipient's email address and Send share link.

The recipient opens a page titled Evidence report shared with you, chooses Email me a verification code, enters the 6-digit code sent to that same address, and then Download report. The share list shows each share's state, such as Waiting for them to verify, Expired or revoked, and Revoke stops a share immediately.

How the link is protected:

  • The link is a locator, not a credential. Opening it reveals nothing until the recipient proves they control the email address.
  • The download token issued after verification is scoped to that one report and expires after 15 minutes.
  • Revoking a share blocks any further code request or verification immediately.
  • Every step (created, code requested, verified, denied, viewed, revoked) is written to the audit trail.

docs.title: Schedules
docs.text:
Schedules → New schedule runs a template automatically:

  • Name, Template to run and Active
  • How often: Every day, Every week, Every 30 days, Every 90 days, or Custom (a cron expression, in UTC)
  • Tell these addresses when it finishes: who is notified when a run completes
  • Also e-mail the report as a secure link → Send the report to: recipients who get the report itself, through the same verified share link as above, never as an attachment

Each schedule shows Next run, Last run, Runs and Failures. Failed runs are retried, and each schedule runs once per period.

docs.title: From code
docs.text:
Generate a report type through the SDK:

types = client.reports.list()        # ids, names, scope and availability
result = client.reports.generate(report_type_id="fairness_audit", model_id=model_id, format="pdf")
html = client.reports.preview(report_type_id="fairness_audit", model_id=model_id)

Report type ids: quarterly_board_pack, iso42001_statement_of_applicability, eu_ai_act_annex_iv_technical_documentation, eu_ai_act_conformity_checklist, gdpr_dpia_automated_decision_record, ccpa_admt_risk_assessment, nist_ai_rmf_profile, model_card, fairness_audit, drift_report, evidence_pack, auditor_traceability_matrix. Take ids from client.reports.list() rather than hard-coding them.

A generated report is an export with an id. To save the file from Python:

from whiteboxxai import ExportFormat

result = client.reports.generate(
    report_type_id="model_card", model_id=model_id, format=ExportFormat.PDF  # PDF, HTML or DOCX
)
client.reports.download(result, path="model_card.pdf")     # writes the file and returns its bytes
# async: await client.reports.agenerate(...); await client.reports.adownload(result, path=...)

Next SDK release

ExportFormat, client.reports.download() and adownload() are in the current development version of the SDK and aren't in the published 1.3.0 yet. Until they ship, pass format="pdf" to generate and download with the endpoint below.

Download, share and sign it through the export endpoints:

# Download
curl -L -o report.pdf https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/export/exports/{export_id}/download \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY"

# Share with an auditor (presets: share_with_auditor, quick_preview)
curl -X POST https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/export/exports/{export_id}/share \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"recipient_email": "auditor@example.com", "preset": "share_with_auditor"}'

# Record a sign-off: "prepared", "reviewed" or "approved"
curl -X POST https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/export/exports/{export_id}/signoffs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"role": "reviewed"}'

Data exports in other formats (CSV, Excel, JSON, Markdown) for model performance, drift, bias, explainability, LLM monitoring, the risk register and the trust score are available from POST /api/v1/export/exports, with schedules under /api/v1/export/scheduled-reports. See the API Reference.

Generating reports, sharing and scheduling don't count as Governance Events.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Is a report a snapshot or live? A snapshot. A generated report records the evidence as it was when generated, so it stays stable for an audit. Generate again, or schedule it, to reflect newer data.

What if part of a report has no data? It says so. An empty, labelled section is more defensible under audit than a filled-in one.

Can an AI assistant generate reports? Yes, through the Python SDK. The MCP server has no report-generation tools. The compliance-assistant prompt tells it to give you the download link and date rather than paraphrase a report it hasn't read.

docs.title: AI Risk Register
docs.text:
The AI Risk Register is a structured inventory of the risks across your model portfolio. Each entry has an owner, a likelihood × impact score, a mitigation plan, and a workflow status — plus a full audit trail of every status change.

This is the artifact auditors ask for by name. ISO/IEC 42001 Clause 6.1 requires documented AI risk assessment and treatment, and the EU AI Act's risk-management obligations for high-risk systems expect the same evidence. The register also gives you a place to map technical controls to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.

In the Enhanced Dashboard it's Risk Register, with three tabs:

  • Register: every risk, with filters. New risk adds one, and auto-drafted entries are badged.
  • Heat map: a 5×5 likelihood × impact grid using your organization's own thresholds, with a plain-language reading. Click a cell to see its open risks.
  • Scales: the likelihood and impact scales, severity thresholds and categories. Everyone can read them; administrators can edit them.

You can also manage it through the REST API. API examples below use the base URL https://api.whiteboxxai.com and an API key (Authorization: Bearer $WHITEBOX_API_KEY).

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
Risk entry — a single identified risk, optionally linked to one or more registered models.

Risk score — likelihood × impact, where each is scored 1–5. The resulting 1–25 score maps to a severity band.

Severity — low, medium, high, or critical, derived from the score using your organization's thresholds.

Owner — the person accountable for the risk. Assigning an owner is what turns a register from a list into a process.

docs.title: Likelihood and impact scales
docs.text:
Both are 1–5. The default labels:

Value Likelihood Impact 1 Rare Negligible 2 Unlikely Minor 3 Possible Moderate 4 Likely Major 5 Almost Certain Severe

docs.title: Severity thresholds
docs.text:
By default, severity is derived from the likelihood × impact score:

Score Severity 20–25 critical 12–19 high 6–11 medium 1–5 low

Both the scale labels and the thresholds are configurable — see Scoring configuration.

docs.title: Categories
docs.text: The default category taxonomy: bias, drift, security, regulatory, operational, reputational, third_party, hallucination, privacy, other. You can replace this list with your own taxonomy on the Scales tab.

docs.title: Workflow states
docs.text:
identified → assessed → mitigation_planned → mitigated → closed

Every status change is written to the audit trail with the user who made it, a timestamp, and a required reason. That history is what makes the register usable as compliance evidence rather than just a tracker.

docs.title: Create a risk entry
docs.text:
In the dashboard, go to Risk Register → New risk, or use the API:

curl -X POST https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/risk-register \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Credit model may under-approve applicants in rural ZIP codes",
    "description": "Fairness audit showed a 9% approval gap by geography.",
    "category": "bias",
    "likelihood": 4,
    "impact": 4,
    "owner_id": "a1b2c3d4-...",
    "mitigation_plan": "Retrain with geographically balanced sampling; re-audit before release.",
    "target_resolution_date": "2026-09-30",
    "review_cadence_days": 30,
    "model_ids": ["11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555"]
  }'

Returns 201 with the created entry, including the computed risk_score (16) and severity (high).

Field reference

Field Notes title Required, max 500 characters. description Optional free text. category Required. Must be in your category taxonomy. likelihood / impact Required, 1–5 each. owner_id Optional user ID accountable for the risk. mitigation_plan Optional free text. target_resolution_date Optional date. review_cadence_days Optional. Sets next_review_at for periodic re-assessment. model_ids Optional list of registered model IDs this risk applies to.

Read-only fields on the response: risk_score, severity, status, next_review_at, source_type, source_id, closed_at, created_by, created_at, updated_at.

docs.title: List and filter entries
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/risk-register?status=identified&category=bias&skip=0&limit=50

The response is paginated:

{
  "items": [ ... ],
  "total": 137,
  "skip": 0,
  "limit": 50
}

Filter by category, model, owner, status, and severity. In the dashboard, the same filters are available above the register table.

docs.title: Update an entry
docs.text:
Send only the fields you want to change:

curl -X PATCH https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/risk-register/{entry_id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "likelihood": 2,
    "mitigation_plan": "Retraining complete; monitoring the approval gap weekly."
  }'

Changing likelihood or impact recomputes risk_score and severity automatically.

docs.title: Moving through the workflow
docs.text:
Status changes go through the same PATCH, but status_reason is required whenever you include status:

curl -X PATCH https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/risk-register/{entry_id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "status": "mitigated",
    "status_reason": "Retrained model v4.1 closed the approval gap to 1.2%; re-audit passed 2026-08-14."
  }'

Omitting status_reason on a status change is rejected. The reason becomes the audit-trail entry — this is deliberate, because "who decided this risk was mitigated, and why" is exactly what an auditor asks.

docs.title: Audit trail
docs.text:
Every create, field edit, and status change is retained:

GET /api/v1/risk-register/{entry_id}/history

{
  "risk_entry_id": "...",
  "events": [
    {
      "event_action": "update",
      "description": "Status changed from mitigation_planned to mitigated",
      "details": { "from": "mitigation_planned", "to": "mitigated" },
      "username": "dana@example.com",
      "created_at": "2026-08-14T16:04:11Z"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Portfolio view and heat map
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/risk-register/portfolio

{
  "heatmap": [ { "likelihood": 4, "impact": 4, "count": 3 }, ... ],
  "top_risks": [ ... ],
  "open_count": 41,
  "open_by_severity": { "critical": 2, "high": 9, "medium": 21, "low": 9 }
}

heatmap is the 5×5 likelihood × impact grid with a count of open risks per cell. top_risks lists the highest-severity open risks, most severe first. The dashboard renders this on the Risk Register → Heat map tab.

docs.title: Automatic risk drafting
docs.text:
A blank register is the most common way a risk process dies. WhiteBoxXAI drafts entries for you when the platform detects something that warrants one. Three rules are active:

Trigger Creates Category Likelihood / Impact A bias audit detects bias at high or critical severity "Bias/fairness threshold breach — model" bias 4 or 5 / 4 A drift report lands at high or critical severity "High-severity drift detected — model" drift 4 or 5 / 3 A governance review request is denied or sent back with request changes "Governance review flagged: title" operational 3 / 3

Auto-drafted entries arrive in identified status with source_type set to bias_audit, drift_report, or governance_review, and source_id pointing at the originating record. They are ordinary entries from there on — assign an owner, adjust the scoring, and work them through the workflow.

No duplicates

If an open entry already exists for the same source record, a repeat trigger is skipped rather than creating a second entry. A flapping drift detector won't flood your register.

docs.title: Scoring configuration
docs.text:
Organization admins can replace the default scales, taxonomy, and thresholds:

GET /api/v1/risk-register/config

{
  "likelihood_scale": [ { "value": 1, "label": "Rare" }, ... ],
  "impact_scale": [ { "value": 1, "label": "Negligible" }, ... ],
  "category_taxonomy": ["bias", "drift", "security", ...],
  "severity_thresholds": { "critical": 20, "high": 12, "medium": 6 },
  "is_default": true
}

is_default: true means your organization has no override on file and is using the defaults documented above. To change them:

PUT /api/v1/risk-register/config
{
  "category_taxonomy": ["bias", "drift", "security", "regulatory", "model_risk"],
  "severity_thresholds": { "critical": 16, "high": 10, "medium": 5 }
}

Send only the parts you want to override. In the dashboard this lives on the Risk Register → Scales tab, where administrators can also rename the likelihood and impact steps.

Changing thresholds re-rates every risk

Saving new severity thresholds re-rates every risk your organization holds, so the register, the heat map and reports stay consistent with the scale you've set. The change is recorded in the audit trail.

docs.title: Evidence exports
docs.text: Risk register data is available as an export category, so the register can be included in the compliance evidence package you hand to an auditor alongside bias audits, drift reports, and governance decisions. See Reports.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Trust Score — the aggregate 0–100 index over fairness, drift, and explainability signals.
  • Governance Review Boards — multi-party approval workflows, one of the three sources that auto-draft risk entries.
  • AI Regulations — background on the wider regulatory landscape.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Settings is in the sidebar footer and the avatar menu. Panes are grouped into You (your own account) and Organisation (shared settings, mostly for administrators). There are 15 panes in all, and each links to its own address, for example ?pane=sso.

docs.title: Profile & security
docs.text:
• Name and avatar
  • Change password
  • Two-factor authentication: turn it on with an authenticator app and save your backup codes. You need it to vote on review requests. See Two-Factor Authentication.
  • Recent activity on your account

docs.title: Preferences
docs.text:
• Layout: New layout (Enhanced) or Classic layout
  • Lens: your default lens
  • Theme: Light, Dark or Match my device
  • Density: Comfortable or Compact

Preferences sync to your account, so they follow you across browsers.

docs.title: Data & privacy
docs.text:
• Marketing emails: opt in or out
  • Download my data: a JSON export of the personal data held about you
  • Delete my account: asks for your password, and an authenticator code if two-factor is on

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
• Delivery Channels: the organization's configured channels (Slack, email, webhook, SMS, PagerDuty) and whether each is enabled. Administrators add and test channels under Integrations.
  • Alert Rules: a summary of how alert rules work, with View and configure Alert Rules, which opens Needs Attention → Alert Rules.
  • Defensible Audit Trail & Governance Notices: how notification activity is recorded.

docs.title: Users & roles
docs.text:
Invite user sends an email invitation with a role: Administrator, Analyst or Viewer. The invitee sets their own password from the link; no password is sent by email. Administrators can change roles and Revoke access. You can't change your own role.

See roles for what each role can do.

docs.title: API keys
docs.text:
Administrators create, view and revoke API keys here. A key is shown once, when it's created; the list shows each key's expiry and when it was last used. Non-administrators see who their administrators are instead.

A key acts with the permissions of the administrator who created it. See API Keys.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
Health cards for GitHub, each notification channel type, the SDK, LLM gateways, ServiceNow AI Control Tower and the MCP server, showing whether each is connected and working. The LLM gateways card covers every connected gateway: it counts the calls recorded across all of them, shows the verdict for the one that most needs attention with that gateway's name, and links to the LLM gateway pane. The ServiceNow card shows status only; records are pulled in from the Evidence page (see ServiceNow AI Control Tower).

Notification channels are where alerts and notifications are delivered: Slack, email, webhook, SMS and PagerDuty. Administrators can add, edit and delete channels, and use Send test to confirm one works before relying on it.

docs.title: Subscription & usage
docs.text:
Your Plan, its Status and when it Renews, and usage this month: N of M Governance Events used. On Business Cloud, usage past the allowance shows as billed as overage. Depending on your plan you'll see Manage billing, Upgrade, or "To change this plan, contact billing".

See Plans & Limits and Governance Events.

docs.title: Trust score weights
docs.text: Administrators set how much fairness, drift and explainability each contribute to the Trust Score. Scores are recalculated on a schedule, so new weights show from the next recalculation.

docs.title: Brand profiles
docs.text: The look of generated reports: colours (with a contrast check), font, cover layout, header and footer text, confidentiality marking, disclaimer, watermark, page size and logo. Keep several profiles and set one as the Default. Administrators edit; everyone else can view. See Reports.

docs.title: Writing style
docs.text: Explains what each lens changes in report wording, and the audience, tone, detail and spelling options report templates use. See Reports.

docs.title: Security posture
docs.text:
For administrators: an at-a-glance view of your organization's access hygiene.

  • Two-factor authentication: the share of users with two-factor turned on
  • API keys: active keys, and stale ones that haven't been used recently
  • Role distribution: how many users hold each role
  • Access review: accounts that look stale, the Last formal review date, and when the next review is due

docs.title: Run an access review
docs.text:
Periodic user access reviews, which auditors routinely ask to see, are run from this pane:

  1. Start Access Review (or Continue In-Progress Review). The review takes a snapshot of active user accounts, with each person's role and whether two-factor authentication is enabled.
  2. For each account, choose Keep or Revoke. Revoking requires a note explaining why.
  3. Add Review Notes / Ledger Summary, for example "Quarterly access review completed by Security Officer".
  4. Complete Access Review. Each decision is recorded as an attestation (retained or revoked), with who reviewed it and when.

A completed access review is filed as evidence through Collect system evidence in Compliance & Evidence.

docs.title: Single sign-on
docs.text: Administrators connect Microsoft Entra ID here so people sign in with their work accounts. The pane covers Connect Microsoft Entra ID, creating accounts on first sign-in, the role given when Microsoft sends none, role mapping from Microsoft app roles, Require SSO and the break-glass administrators who keep password sign-in. It is available on Business Cloud and above; on the Free plan the pane says so. See Single Sign-On.

docs.title: LLM gateway
docs.text:
Administrators connect their organisation's LiteLLM gateway here once. LiteLLM then sends every call through it to WhiteBoxXAI, which files each under the AI system it belongs to. The pane shows a verdict in words (receiving, gone quiet, calls being lost), what is stored from each call and what redaction misses, the configuration to paste into LiteLLM, the traffic no rule has claimed so you can assign it to an AI system, and the controls to rotate the token, switch acceptance off or disconnect. Non-administrators are told that administrators manage it.

The pane opens on the LiteLLM tab. It also has tabs for OpenTelemetry (OTLP), Portkey AI, Kong AI Gateway and Azure APIM; each gateway is a separate connection with its own token. Each tab says what its gateway sends and, when you connect, where that gateway takes the token.

See LiteLLM gateway and LLM gateways.

docs.title: Sample data & tour
docs.text:
• Load sample data: fill your account with clearly marked sample models, predictions, drift events, audits and reports. Sample-data models don't count against your plan.
  • Reset sample data: remove them (it asks you to confirm)
  • Product tour: replay the guided tour

docs.title: Trust Score
docs.text:
The Trust Score is a single 0–100 index per model, combining three signals WhiteBoxXAI already computes: the model's latest bias/fairness audit, its current drift severity, and how much of its prediction volume has been explained.

It exists so a non-technical stakeholder — a board, a risk committee, an executive sponsor — can assess a model at a glance and then drill into what drove the number. The methodology is documented in full below on purpose: an unexplainable trustworthiness score would be a strange thing for an explainability platform to ship.

API examples use the base URL https://api.whiteboxxai.com and require an API key (Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY).

docs.title: How the score is calculated
docs.text: Three components, each normalized to 0–100, then combined as a weighted average.

docs.title: Fairness component
docs.text: Taken from the model's most recent bias/fairness audit. A model whose latest audit shows no detected bias scores at the top of this component; higher-severity findings pull it down.

docs.title: Drift component
docs.text:
Taken from the model's worst current drift severity:

Drift severity Component score None 100 Low 80 Medium 55 High 25 Critical 0

docs.title: Explainability component
docs.text: The ratio of the model's logged predictions that have a generated explanation. A model with explanations on most of its traffic scores high; one with none scores at the bottom. This is coverage, not explanation quality.

docs.title: Weighting
docs.text:
The three components are combined using your organization's configured weights. The defaults:

Component Default weight Fairness 0.4 Drift 0.3 Explainability 0.3

Weights are renormalized over whichever inputs actually exist. A model with no bias audit yet still gets a score from drift and explainability alone, with those two weights scaled back up to sum to 1. This matters when you're onboarding: a new model isn't punished with a low score for evidence it hasn't had time to produce.

A model with none of the three inputs has no score at all — trust_score is null, and the model is counted in models_with_insufficient_data rather than dragging down your portfolio average.

Scores are recalculated on a schedule

Trust Scores are computed by a scheduled background job and stored as snapshots, not recalculated on every prediction. A fresh bias audit or drift report will be reflected in the score on the next run, which is also what makes the history endpoint meaningful.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Surface What it shows Overview The Average trust score tile, and its trend on the Trends tab Model Register A Trust score column, and Trust score history with its three components in each system's dossier Settings → Trust score weights Weight configuration (administrators) Reports Trust Score in the Quarterly Board Pack and Evidence Pack

docs.title: Get one model's score
docs.text:
curl https://api.whiteboxxai.com/api/v1/trust-score/{model_id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"

{
  "model_id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
  "model_name": "fraud-detection-v3",
  "trust_score": 78.5,
  "fairness_component": 85.0,
  "drift_component": 80.0,
  "explainability_component": 66.0,
  "inputs_available": {
    "fairness": true,
    "drift": true,
    "explainability": true
  },
  "last_bias_audit_at": "2026-07-21T09:12:00Z",
  "last_drift_report_at": "2026-07-28T02:00:00Z",
  "explained_predictions_ratio": 0.66,
  "weights": { "fairness": 0.4, "drift": 0.3, "explainability": 0.3 },
  "methodology_note": "Trust Score = weighted average of fairness (bias audit), drift severity, and explainability coverage, renormalized over whichever inputs are available for this model, using this organization's configured (or default) component weights."
}

inputs_available tells you which of the three signals contributed. Use it to explain a score to a stakeholder — a 78.5 built from two of three components is a different statement than one built from all three.

docs.title: Portfolio rollup
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/trust-score/portfolio

{
  "org_average_trust_score": 81.2,
  "models": [ { "model_id": "...", "model_name": "...", "trust_score": 78.5, ... } ],
  "models_with_insufficient_data": 2,
  "methodology_note": "..."
}

This is what backs the Executive Dashboard gauge. models_with_insufficient_data counts models excluded from the average because none of the three inputs exist yet — worth surfacing in a board conversation rather than hiding.

docs.title: Score history
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/trust-score/{model_id}/history

{
  "model_id": "...",
  "data_points": [
    {
      "snapshot_at": "2026-07-01T00:00:00Z",
      "trust_score": 72.0,
      "fairness_component": 75.0,
      "drift_component": 80.0,
      "explainability_component": 60.0
    }
  ],
  "trend_direction": "improving"
}

trend_direction is improving, declining, or stable, and is null until there are at least two snapshots. Because each snapshot keeps the component values, you can see which component moved — a declining score driven by drift is a different problem from one driven by falling explanation coverage.

docs.title: Configure the weights
docs.text:
Organization admins can reweight the components to match their own risk priorities:

GET /api/v1/trust-score/config

{
  "fairness_weight": 0.4,
  "drift_weight": 0.3,
  "explainability_weight": 0.3,
  "is_default": true
}

is_default: true means no override is on file and the defaults above are in use. To change them:

PUT /api/v1/trust-score/config
{
  "fairness_weight": 0.5,
  "drift_weight": 0.3,
  "explainability_weight": 0.2
}

In the dashboard this lives at Settings → Trust score weights.

Document your weighting

If you reweight, record why. A score is only defensible in an audit if the methodology behind it is deliberate and written down — the same reason the default weights are published on this page rather than buried in code.

docs.title: Not in scope
docs.text:
Two things the Trust Score deliberately doesn't do:

  • Peer benchmarking. There's no "compare your score to your industry" — no dataset exists to support that claim honestly.
  • Automated enforcement. A low score doesn't pause a model or block a deployment. Acting on the score is a human decision, routed through Governance Review Boards if you want approval gates.
